A year has 12 months: big months have 31 days (January, March, May, July, August, October, December), small months have 30 days (April, June, September, November), and February has 28 days in a common year and 29 in a leap year
Leap years: a year divisible by 4 is usually a leap year, but a century year must be divisible by 400 — so 1900 is not a leap year and 2000 is
A common year has 365 days and a leap year 366; convert as with length: big to small multiply, small to big divide, e.g. 180 min = 3 h

examples.problem: 妈妈买了一箱牛奶，每盒牛奶重 250 克，一箱有 24 盒。这箱牛奶一共重多少克？合多少千克？
examples.solution: 总质量 $=250\times 24=6000$（克）。千克和克之间的进率是 1000，小单位化大单位要除以进率：$6000\div 1000=6$（千克）。验算：$6\times 1000=6000$ ✓。

examples.problem: 判断下面这些年份是不是闰年，并说出这一年二月有多少天：（1）2024 年；（2）1900 年；（3）2000 年。

solid-figures-elementary.definition:
我们身边到处都是立体图形：牙膏盒、鞋盒是**长方体**，魔方、骰子是**正方体**，饮料罐、笔筒是**圆柱**，皮球、地球仪是**球**。它们都占一定的空间，这就是「立体的」。

长方体上平平的部分叫**面**，两个面相交的边叫**棱**，三条棱相交的点叫**顶点**。数一数：长方体有 **6 个面**、**12 条棱**、**8 个顶点**，可以记成口诀「六面十二棱八顶点」。正方体的 6 个面都是完全相同的正方形，12 条棱长度都相等——所以**正方体是特殊的长方体**，就像正方形是特殊的长方形一样。

圆柱上下有 **2 个底面**，是两个同样大的圆；周围是 **1 个侧面**，是弯弯的**曲面**。球最特别：它的表面全是曲面，**没有平面**，也没有棱和顶点，往哪个方向都能滚。
solid-figures-elementary.definitionEn:
Solid figures are all around us: a toothpaste box or a shoe box is a **cuboid**, a die or a Rubik's cube is a **cube**, a drink can is a **cylinder**, and a ball is a **sphere**. They all take up space — that is what makes them solid.

The flat parts of a cuboid are its **faces**, the edges where two faces meet are its **edges**, and the points where three edges meet are its **vertices**. Count them: a cuboid has **6 faces**, **12 edges** and **8 vertices**. A cube has 6 identical square faces and 12 equal edges, so **a cube is a special cuboid**, just as a square is a special rectangle.

A cylinder has **2 bases**, two congruent circles, and **1 curved side**. A sphere is even more special: its whole surface is curved, with **no flat face**, no edges and no vertices, so it rolls in every direction.
derivation: 立体图形占有空间。围成立体图形的各个面叫做面；两个面相交的线段叫做棱；几条棱相交的点叫做顶点。面可以是平面，也可以是曲面。长方体、正方体、圆柱和球是小学常见的立体图形，它们的面、棱、顶点数目并非各不相同；例如长方体和正方体都是 6 个面、12 条棱、8 个顶点，而圆柱、球的面数不同。
长方体有 $6$ 个面，分成 $3$ 组相对的面，每组两个面完全相同；有 $12$ 条棱，分成 $3$ 组，每组 $4$ 条棱互相平行且长度相等；有 $8$ 个顶点。验算：每个顶点连着 $3$ 条棱，$8\times3=24$；每条棱有 $2$ 个端点，$12\times2=24$，两种数法一致。
正方体的 $6$ 个面都是完全相同的正方形，$12$ 条棱长度都相等，也有 $8$ 个顶点。因此正方体满足长方体的全部特征，是特殊的长方体，记作正方体 $\subset$ 长方体。但长方体不一定 $6$ 个面都是正方形，所以反过来不成立。
圆柱有 $2$ 个同样大的圆形底面，它们互相平行；还有 $1$ 个弯曲的侧面。两个底面圆周是侧面与底面的交界线，但它们不是两个平面相交形成的棱；圆柱没有顶点。把圆柱的侧面沿高剪开展平，得到一个长方形，它的长等于底面周长，宽等于圆柱的高。
球的表面全部是曲面，没有平面，没有棱，也没有顶点；从球心到球面上任意一点的距离都相等。球放在平面上只与平面接触于一点，因此能向任意方向滚动。圆柱虽然也能滚动，但它有 $2$ 个平面底面，放倒后只能沿一个方向滚动，两者结构不同。
数面、棱、顶点时要注意「面」包括曲面：圆柱是 $3$ 个面（$2$ 个平面、$1$ 个曲面），不是 $2$ 个面；球是 $1$ 个曲面，不是 $0$ 个面。仅凭「会滚」不能判断图形，仅凭面数也不能区分长方体与正方体；还要结合面的形状、大小以及棱长关系来判断。
derivationEn: A solid figure occupies space. Each surface enclosing it is called a face; a segment where two faces meet is an edge; a point where several edges meet is a vertex. A face may be flat or curved. Cuboids, cubes, cylinders and spheres are common solids in primary school, and their numbers of faces, edges and vertices are not all different: a cuboid and a cube both have 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.

A cuboid has $6$ faces in $3$ pairs of opposite faces, the two faces in each pair being identical; it has $12$ edges in $3$ groups of $4$ parallel equal edges; and it has $8$ vertices. Check: each vertex lies on $3$ edges, giving $8\times3=24$; each edge has $2$ endpoints, giving $12\times2=24$. The two counts agree.

A cube has $6$ faces that are all identical squares, $12$ edges of equal length, and $8$ vertices. Hence a cube satisfies every property of a cuboid and is a special cuboid, written cube $\subset$ cuboid. A cuboid, however, need not have six square faces, so the converse does not hold.

A cylinder has $2$ equal circular bases that are parallel to each other, and $1$ curved lateral surface. The two base circles are the boundary curves where the lateral surface meets the bases, but they are not edges formed by two intersecting planes; a cylinder has no vertex. Cutting the lateral surface along a height and unrolling it gives a rectangle whose length is the base circumference and whose width is the height.

The whole surface of a sphere is curved: it has no flat face, no edge and no vertex, and every point on the surface is at the same distance from the centre. A sphere touches a plane at a single point, so it can roll in any direction. A cylinder can also roll, but it has $2$ flat circular bases and, when laid on its side, rolls in only one direction; the two solids are structurally different.

When counting faces, edges and vertices, remember that a face may be curved: a cylinder has $3$ faces ($2$ flat and $1$ curved), not $2$; a sphere has $1$ curved surface, not $0$ faces. Being able to roll does not identify a solid, and the number of faces alone does not distinguish a cuboid from a cube; the shapes and sizes of the faces and the edge lengths must also be considered.

formulas.note: 长方体有 6 个面、12 条棱、8 个顶点，口诀是「六面十二棱八顶点」；正方体也一样。
formulas.noteEn: A cuboid has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices (a cube has the same counts).

formulas.note: 每个顶点连着 3 条棱，每条棱连着 2 个顶点——8×3 和 12×2 正好相等，数完可以这样验算。
formulas.noteEn: Each vertex joins 3 edges and each edge joins 2 vertices, so 8×3 = 12×2 — a handy double-check when counting.

formulas.note: 正方体是特殊的长方体：6 个面都是完全相同的正方形，12 条棱长度都相等。
formulas.noteEn: A cube is a special cuboid: its 6 faces are identical squares and its 12 edges are equal.

formulas.note: 圆柱有 2 个同样大的圆形底面和 1 个曲面侧面，所以放倒后能滚动。
formulas.noteEn: A cylinder has 2 congruent circular bases and 1 curved side, so it can roll.

formulas.latex: \text{球} : \text{没有平面，也没有棱和顶点}
formulas.note: 球的表面全是曲面，朝任何方向都能滚。
formulas.noteEn: A sphere's surface is all curved — no flat face, no edges, no vertices.

properties: 长方体有 6 个面、12 条棱、8 个顶点；正方体也有 6 个面、12 条棱、8 个顶点
正方体是特殊的长方体：它的 6 个面都是完全相同的正方形，12 条棱长度都相等
圆柱有 2 个同样大的圆形底面和 1 个曲面侧面，放倒后可以滚动
球没有平面，没有棱和顶点，在任何方向都能滚动
propertiesEn: A cuboid has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices; a cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices too
A cube is a special cuboid: its 6 faces are identical squares and its 12 edges are equal
A cylinder has 2 congruent circular bases and 1 curved side; laid on its side it can roll
A sphere has no flat face, no edges and no vertices, and it rolls in every direction

examples.problem: 数一数：一个长方体饼干盒有几个面、几条棱、几个顶点？如果它的长、宽、高都变成 6 厘米，它变成了什么图形？
examples.solution: 长方体有 6 个面、12 条棱、8 个顶点，记成口诀「六面十二棱八顶点」。当长、宽、高都是 6 厘米时，6 个面都成了完全相同的正方形，12 条棱也一样长，它就变成了**正方体**——正方形是特殊的长方形，正方体是特殊的长方体。

examples.problem: 小明说：「皮球和易拉罐都会滚，它们差不多。」他说得对吗？请分别说说它们各有几个平面。
examples.solution: 不对。易拉罐是**圆柱**：有 2 个同样大的圆形底面，1 个侧面是曲面，它只能沿着一个方向滚；皮球是**球**：表面全是曲面，没有平面，朝哪个方向都能滚。它们的面完全不同，不是「差不多」。

expression.text: 长方体：6 个面、12 条棱、8 个顶点；正方体是特殊的长方体
expression.note: 数面、数棱时可以按「上下、前后、左右」一对一对地数，就不会漏。
expression.noteEn: Count faces and edges in pairs (top-bottom, front-back, left-right) so that nothing is missed.

angles-elementary.definition:
从一点引出两条**射线**，就组成一个**角**。这个点叫角的**顶点**，两条射线叫角的**两条边**。角也可以看成一条射线绕它的端点旋转形成的图形。

角的大小只跟两条边**张开的程度**有关，跟两条边画得**长还是短没有关系**——把边画得再长，角也一点都不会变大！比较两个角时，要把顶点对齐、一条边重合，再看另一条边张开得大不大。

量角要用**量角器**，角的单位是**度**，记作「°」：把半圆平均分成 180 份，每一份所对的角就是 1 度（1°）。按大小分类：小于 90° 的叫**锐角**，等于 90° 的叫**直角**，大于 90° 而小于 180° 的叫**钝角**；两条边成一条直线时是**平角**（180°），绕一圈回到原处是**周角**（360°）。所以 1 平角 = 2 直角，1 周角 = 2 平角 = 4 直角。
angles-elementary.definitionEn:
Two **rays** drawn from one point form an **angle**. The point is the **vertex**, and the two rays are the **sides** of the angle. An angle can also be seen as what a ray sweeps out while it turns about its endpoint.

The size of an angle depends only on how wide its two sides are **open**, and never on how long the sides are drawn — making the sides longer does not make the angle bigger! To compare two angles, put their vertices together, make one pair of sides overlap, and look at how widely the other pair opens.

We measure angles with a **protractor**, in **degrees**, written °: divide a half circle into 180 equal parts, and each part is 1 degree (1°). By size: an angle smaller than 90° is **acute**, one equal to 90° is a **right angle**, and one greater than 90° but less than 180° is **obtuse**. When the two sides form a straight line, the angle is a **straight angle** (180°), and one full turn gives a **full angle** (360°). Hence 1 straight angle = 2 right angles, and 1 full angle = 2 straight angles = 4 right angles.
derivation: 从一点引出两条射线就组成一个角：这个点是顶点，两条射线是角的两条边。角也可以看成一条射线绕端点旋转形成的图形。角的大小只由两条边张开的程度决定，与边画得多长无关；比较两个角时，把顶点对齐、一条边重合，再看另一条边张开的大小。
把一个周角（一整圈）平均分成 360 份，每一份所对的角就是 1 度，记作 $1^\circ$。因此周角是 $360^\circ$，平角（两条边成一条直线）是 $180^\circ$，直角是 $90^\circ$。度以下还有分、秒：$1^\circ=60'$，$1'=60''$，是六十进制，不是十进制。

按大小分类：$0^\circ<\alpha<90^\circ$ 是锐角，$\alpha=90^\circ$ 是直角，$90^\circ<\alpha<180^\circ$ 是钝角，$\alpha=180^\circ$ 是平角，$\alpha=360^\circ$ 是周角。边界要分清：等于 90° 的角不能叫锐角，等于 180° 的角也不能叫钝角；0° 与 360° 的两条边重合，但表示的旋转程度不同。
由定义直接得到：$1$ 平角 $=180^\circ=2\times90^\circ=2$ 直角；$1$ 周角 $=360^\circ=2\times180^\circ=2$ 平角 $=4$ 直角。反过来，半个平角是 $90^\circ$，恰好是一个直角；四分之一个周角也是 $90^\circ$。这些关系常用来验算量角结果。
量角器是半圆，把半圆平均分成 180 份，每份 $1^\circ$。量角时做到「中心对顶点、零刻度线对一边」，另一条边所对的刻度就是角的度数；量角器有内、外两圈刻度，先看零刻度线用的是哪一圈，再读同一圈。若一条边没有对准零刻度，就用两条边读数之差计算，例如 $125^\circ-65^\circ=60^\circ$。
角的加减用六十进制：$35^\circ40'+25^\circ35'=60^\circ75'=61^\circ15'$，因为 $75'=60'+15'=1^\circ15'$。两个角相加得 $90^\circ$ 时互为余角，相加得 $180^\circ$ 时互为补角；例如 $35^\circ$ 的余角是 $55^\circ$，补角是 $145^\circ$。
derivationEn: Two rays drawn from one point form an angle: the point is the vertex and the rays are its sides. An angle can also be viewed as what a ray sweeps out while rotating about its endpoint. Its size depends only on how widely the sides open, not on how long they are drawn; to compare two angles, align the vertices and one pair of sides, then compare the openings.

Divide a full turn into 360 equal parts; the angle subtended by one part is 1 degree, written $1^\circ$. Hence a full angle is $360^\circ$, a straight angle (whose sides form a line) is $180^\circ$, and a right angle is $90^\circ$. Below degrees are minutes and seconds: $1^\circ=60'$ and $1'=60''$, a sexagesimal rather than decimal system.

By size: $0^\circ<\alpha<90^\circ$ is acute, $\alpha=90^\circ$ is right, $90^\circ<\alpha<180^\circ$ is obtuse, $\alpha=180^\circ$ is straight, and $\alpha=360^\circ$ is full. Mind the boundaries: an angle equal to 90° is not acute, and one equal to 180° is not obtuse; at 0° and 360° the sides coincide, but the amounts of rotation differ.

The definitions give $1$ straight angle $=180^\circ=2\times90^\circ=2$ right angles, and $1$ full angle $=360^\circ=2\times180^\circ=2$ straight angles $=4$ right angles. Conversely, half a straight angle is $90^\circ$, exactly one right angle, and a quarter of a full angle is also $90^\circ$. These relations serve as checks on protractor readings.

A protractor is a semicircle divided into 180 equal parts, each $1^\circ$. To measure, place the centre on the vertex and the zero line along one side; the mark met by the other side gives the angle. A protractor has inner and outer scales, so first note which zero line is used and read the same scale. If a side is not on zero, subtract the two readings, e.g. $125^\circ-65^\circ=60^\circ$.

Add and subtract angles in sexagesimal form: $35^\circ40'+25^\circ35'=60^\circ75'=61^\circ15'$, because $75'=60'+15'=1^\circ15'$. Two angles are complementary when they sum to $90^\circ$ and supplementary when they sum to $180^\circ$; for example, $35^\circ$ has complement $55^\circ$ and supplement $145^\circ$.

formulas.note: 锐角：比直角小的角，开口比直角窄。
formulas.noteEn: Acute angle: smaller than a right angle.

formulas.note: 直角：可以拿三角尺上的直角去比一比，正好重合就是直角。
formulas.noteEn: Right angle: compare with the right angle of a set square — if they fit exactly, it is a right angle.

formulas.note: 钝角：比直角大，但又比平角小。
formulas.noteEn: Obtuse angle: greater than a right angle but smaller than a straight angle.

formulas.note: 两条边成一条直线，就是平角。1 平角 = 2 直角。
formulas.noteEn: When the two sides form a straight line we get a straight angle; 1 straight angle = 2 right angles.

formulas.note: 一条射线绕端点转一圈，就是周角。1 周角 = 2 平角 = 4 直角。
formulas.noteEn: One full turn of a ray about its endpoint gives a full angle; 1 full angle = 2 straight angles = 4 right angles.

properties: 角有一个顶点、两条边，两条边都是射线
角的大小只与两条边张开的程度有关，与两条边画得长短无关
量角口诀：中心对顶点，零刻度线对一条边，另一条边对着的刻度就是这个角的度数
propertiesEn: An angle has one vertex and two sides, and both sides are rays
The size of an angle depends only on how widely its sides open, not on how long they are drawn
Acute < 90°, right = 90°, and 90° < obtuse < 180°
1 straight angle = 2 right angles = 180°; 1 full angle = 2 straight angles = 4 right angles = 360°
Protractor rule: centre on the vertex, zero line along one side, and read the mark on the other side

examples.problem: 把角的两条边都画成原来的 2 倍长，角变大了吗？1 个周角等于几个直角？半个平角是多少度？
examples.solution: 角没有变大。角的大小只跟两条边张开的程度有关，与边画得长短无关。1 周角 = 360°，1 直角 = 90°，360° ÷ 90° = 4，所以 1 周角 = 2 平角 = 4 直角；半个平角是 180° ÷ 2 = 90°，正好是一个直角。

expression.text: 角 AOB 记作 ∠AOB；∠AOB = 90° 表示它是直角
expression.note: 角可以用三个大写字母表示（顶点字母写在中间），也可以用「∠1」这样的数字来表示。
expression.noteEn: An angle can be named by three capital letters with the vertex in the middle, or by a label such as ∠1.

perimeter-elementary.definition:
沿着操场跑一圈，这一圈的长度就是操场的**周长**。说得准确一点：**封闭图形一周的长度**，叫做它的**周长**。

要算周长，就把围成这个图形的每一条边都加起来。长方形有 2 条长、2 条宽，所以**长方形的周长 =（长 + 宽）× 2**；正方形的 4 条边一样长，所以**正方形的周长 = 边长 × 4**；三角形的周长就是三条边长度之和。

要特别注意：周长的单位是**长度单位**（厘米、分米、米……），它是一条「线」的长度，不是图形里面有多大。算组合图形的周长时，要把最外面一圈的边全部加起来，一条也不能漏。
perimeter-elementary.definitionEn:
Walk one full lap around a playground: the distance you cover is its **perimeter**. More exactly, the **perimeter** of a closed figure is the length of its whole boundary.

To find it, add up every side of the figure. A rectangle has 2 lengths and 2 widths, so **perimeter = (length + width) × 2**; a square has 4 equal sides, so **perimeter = side × 4**; for a triangle it is simply the sum of its three sides.

Remember: a perimeter is measured in **units of length** (cm, dm, m …). It is how long the boundary is, not how large the inside is. For a combined figure, add up the whole outer boundary — not a single side may be missed.
derivation: 封闭图形一周的长度叫做它的周长。对多边形，周长等于所有边长之和：$C=a+b+c+\cdots$，单位是厘米、分米、米等长度单位。只有封闭图形才有确定的周长；不封闭的折线只有长度，不能称为周长。
长方形对边相等。设长为 $a$、宽为 $b$，四条边依次为 $a,b,a,b$，所以 $C=a+b+a+b=2(a+b)$。反过来，已知周长 $C$ 和宽 $b$，则 $a=\frac{C}{2}-b$，因为 $\frac{C}{2}=a+b$ 正好是一条长与一条宽的和。
正方形四条边都等于 $a$，所以 $C=4a$；反过来 $a=\frac{C}{4}$。例如用一根长 $36$ 厘米的铁丝围成一个正方形（接头处忽略不计），边长是 $36\div4=9$ 厘米。这里铁丝的总长度被四条相等的边平分。
三角形的周长是三边之和 $C=a+b+c$；一般多边形逐边相加。求组合图形的周长时，只加最外面一圈的边，内部的分割线不是周长的一部分。把两个图形拼在一起时，拼合处被遮住，不再计入外边界。
周长与面积是两种不同的量：周长是一维边界的长度，面积是二维区域的大小。周长相等的图形面积不一定相等，例如 $8\times2$ 的长方形与边长为 $5$ 的正方形周长都为 $20$，面积分别为 $16$ 与 $25$。因此不能由周长直接判断面积，也不能把长度单位与面积单位混用。
例：长方形花坛长 $8$ 米、宽 $5$ 米，沿花坛走一圈的路程是 $C=2(8+5)=26$ 米。若篱笆总长 $26$ 米且宽为 $5$ 米，则长 $=\frac{26}{2}-5=8$ 米。计算时应先统一单位，再代入公式。
derivationEn: The perimeter of a closed figure is the distance all the way round it. For a polygon it equals the sum of all side lengths, $C=a+b+c+\cdots$, measured in centimetres, decimetres, metres and other length units. Only a closed figure has a definite perimeter; an open broken line has a length but not a perimeter.

Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal. With length $a$ and width $b$, the four sides are $a,b,a,b$, so $C=a+b+a+b=2(a+b)$. Conversely, given the perimeter $C$ and the width $b$, we get $a=\frac{C}{2}-b$, because $\frac{C}{2}=a+b$ is exactly one length plus one width.

All four sides of a square equal $a$, so $C=4a$; conversely $a=\frac{C}{4}$. For example, a $36$ cm wire bent into a square (ignoring the join) gives side $36\div4=9$ cm. The total length of the wire is divided equally among the four sides.

The perimeter of a triangle is the sum of its three sides, $C=a+b+c$; for a general polygon, add all sides. For a composite figure, add only the edges on the outer boundary; internal dividing lines are not part of the perimeter. When two figures are joined, the joined part is hidden and no longer counts as outer boundary.

Perimeter and area are different quantities: perimeter is the one-dimensional length of the boundary, while area is the size of the two-dimensional region. Figures with equal perimeters need not have equal areas: an $8\times2$ rectangle and a square of side $5$ both have perimeter $20$, but their areas are $16$ and $25$. Hence perimeter alone cannot determine area, and length units must not be mixed with area units.

Example: a rectangular flower bed is $8$ m long and $5$ m wide; walking once around it covers $C=2(8+5)=26$ m. If a fence of total length $26$ m has width $5$ m, then its length is $\frac{26}{2}-5=8$ m. Convert all lengths to the same unit before substituting into the formula.

formulas.note: 长方形的周长 =（长 + 宽）× 2，也就是两条长加两条宽。
formulas.noteEn: Rectangle: perimeter = (length + width) × 2, that is, two lengths plus two widths.

formulas.note: 正方形的周长 = 边长 × 4，因为四条边一样长。
formulas.noteEn: Square: perimeter = side × 4, because all four sides are equal.

formulas.note: 三角形的周长就是三条边的长度相加。
formulas.noteEn: Triangle: perimeter = the sum of its three sides.

formulas.note: 反过来用：已知正方形的周长，边长 = 周长 ÷ 4。
formulas.noteEn: Working backwards: side of a square = perimeter ÷ 4.

formulas.note: 已知长方形的周长和宽，长 = 周长 ÷ 2 − 宽（周长的一半是一条长加一条宽）。
formulas.noteEn: For a rectangle, length = perimeter ÷ 2 − width (half the perimeter is one length plus one width).

properties: 周长是封闭图形一周的长度，单位是长度单位：厘米、分米、米……
长方形周长 =（长 + 宽）× 2；正方形周长 = 边长 × 4
已知周长求边长：正方形的边长 = 周长 ÷ 4；长方形的长 = 周长 ÷ 2 − 宽
算组合图形的周长时，要把最外面一圈的边全部加起来，一条都不能漏
propertiesEn: A perimeter is the length of the boundary of a closed figure, measured in units of length: cm, dm, m …
Rectangle: perimeter = (length + width) × 2; square: perimeter = side × 4
Working backwards: side of a square = perimeter ÷ 4; length of a rectangle = perimeter ÷ 2 − width
For a combined figure, add up the whole outer boundary without missing any side

examples.problem: 学校有一个长方形花坛，长 8 米、宽 5 米。沿着花坛走一圈，一共走多少米？
一根 36 厘米长的铁丝，正好围成一个正方形（接头处忽略不计）。这个正方形的边长是多少厘米？
examples.solution: 正方形周长 = 边长 × 4，反过来：边长 = 周长 ÷ 4 = 36 ÷ 4 = 9（厘米）。答：这个正方形的边长是 9 厘米。

expression.text: 长方形周长 C =（长 + 宽）× 2；正方形周长 C = 边长 × 4
expression.note: 周长常用字母 C 表示，长和宽分别用 a、b 表示。
expression.noteEn: The perimeter is often written C, with a and b for length and width.

area-elementary.definition:
摸一摸课桌的桌面和课本的封面，哪个大？比面的大小，比的就是**面积**——**物体的表面或封闭图形的大小**，叫做它们的**面积**。常用的面积单位有**平方厘米、平方分米、平方米**：边长 1 厘米的正方形，面积就是 1 平方厘米。

长方形的面积怎么算？用 1 平方厘米的小正方形去摆：每行摆「长」个，一共摆「宽」行，一共摆了 长 × 宽 个，所以**长方形面积 = 长 × 宽**；正方形是特殊的长方形，**正方形面积 = 边长 × 边长**。

其他图形都可以「变身」成学过的图形：沿着高把平行四边形剪开再平移，正好拼成长方形，所以**平行四边形面积 = 底 × 高**；两个**完全一样**的三角形能拼成一个平行四边形，所以**三角形面积 = 底 × 高 ÷ 2**——**这个「÷ 2」千万不能忘**；两个完全一样的梯形也能拼成平行四边形，所以**梯形面积 =（上底 + 下底）× 高 ÷ 2**。遇到组合图形，可以用「分割」或「添补」的办法，把它变成上面这些图形再求面积。
area-elementary.definitionEn:
Compare a desk top with the cover of a book — which is bigger? Comparing surfaces means comparing **areas**: the **area** of an object's surface, or of a closed figure, tells how large it is. Common units are **square centimetres, square decimetres and square metres**: a square of side 1 cm has area 1 cm².

How do we measure a rectangle? Tile it with 1 cm² squares: 「length」 squares in each row, 「width」 rows in all, so **area = length × width**. A square is a special rectangle, so **area = side × side**.

Every other shape can be turned into one we know. Cut a parallelogram along a height, slide the piece over, and it becomes a rectangle, so **area = base × height**. Two **identical** triangles make a parallelogram, so **area = base × height ÷ 2** — never forget that ÷2! Two identical trapezoids also make a parallelogram, so **area = (upper base + lower base) × height ÷ 2**. For a combined figure, split it up or fill it out into these shapes first.
derivation: 面积是物体表面或封闭图形内部区域的大小。规定边长为 $1$ 厘米的正方形面积为 $1$ 平方厘米，面积用平方厘米、平方分米、平方米等面积单位度量。它度量的是二维区域的大小；周长度量的是围成一圈的边的总长，二者单位不同（平方单位与长度单位），不能直接比较数值大小。
把长方形划分成边长为 $1$ 的小正方形网格：设 $a,b$ 为正整数（使用同一长度单位）；若长为 $a$、宽为 $b$，每一行有 $a$ 个，共有 $b$ 行，所以小正方形的总数为 $a\times b$。因此 $S_{\text{长方形}}=ab$。当 $a=b$ 时得到正方形，$S=a^2$；结果的单位是对应的平方单位。
设平行四边形的底为 $a$，这条底对应的高为 $h$，即 $h$ 与底垂直。沿高剪下一个直角三角形，把它平移到另一侧，恰好补成一个长为 $a$、宽为 $h$ 的长方形；剪拼只改变位置，不改变面积。因此 $S_{\text{平行四边形}}=ah$。注意高必须垂直于所选的底，不能用邻边代替高。
取两个与已知三角形完全一样的三角形（对应边相等），把其中一个旋转 $180^\circ$ 后与另一个拼合，得到底为 $a$、高为 $h$ 的平行四边形。平行四边形面积是 $ah$，两个三角形面积相等，所以每个三角形的面积 $S=\frac{1}{2}ah$。若两个三角形只是相似而不全等，就不能拼成这个平行四边形。
设梯形的上底、下底分别为 $a,b$，高为 $h$，即两底之间的垂直距离。取两个完全一样的梯形，把其中一个旋转 $180^\circ$ 后拼在一起，得到底为 $a+b$、高为 $h$ 的平行四边形。于是 $2S=(a+b)h$，即 $S=\frac{(a+b)h}{2}$。上底、下底必须是互相平行的那两条边。
面积单位换算按长度单位进率的平方：$1\text{ m}^2=100\text{ dm}^2$，$1\text{ dm}^2=100\text{ cm}^2$。组合图形可以用分割或添补的方法转化为上述基本图形再求和。还要注意：周长相同不能推出面积相同，例如长 $8$、宽 $2$ 与边长 $5$ 的正方形周长都是 $20$，面积却分别为 $16$ 和 $25$。
derivationEn: Area is the size of the region inside a surface or a closed figure. A square of side $1$ cm has area $1\text{ cm}^2$, and area is measured in square centimetres, square decimetres, square metres, and so on. Area measures a two-dimensional region, whereas perimeter measures the total length of the boundary; their units differ (square units versus length units), so the two numerical values cannot be compared directly.

Divide a rectangle into a grid of unit squares of side $1$: Assume $a,b$ are positive integers in the chosen unit; if the length is $a$ and the width is $b$, each row contains $a$ squares and there are $b$ rows, so the total number of squares is $a\times b$. Hence $S_{\text{rectangle}}=ab$. When $a=b$ the rectangle is a square and $S=a^2$; the unit of the result is the corresponding square unit.

Let a parallelogram have base $a$ and let $h$ be the height corresponding to this base, so $h$ is perpendicular to the base. Cut off a right triangle along the height and translate it to the other side; it exactly completes a rectangle of length $a$ and width $h$. Cutting and translating change only position, not area, so $S_{\text{parallelogram}}=ah$. The height must be perpendicular to the chosen base; a neighbouring side cannot replace the height.

Take two triangles exactly congruent to the given triangle (all corresponding sides equal), rotate one through $180^\circ$, and fit it with the other to form a parallelogram with base $a$ and height $h$. The parallelogram has area $ah$, and the two triangles have equal areas, so each triangle has area $S=\frac{1}{2}ah$. If the two triangles are merely similar but not congruent, they cannot form this parallelogram.

Let a trapezoid have upper base $a$, lower base $b$ and height $h$, the perpendicular distance between the two bases. Take two identical trapezoids, rotate one through $180^\circ$ and join them to form a parallelogram with base $a+b$ and height $h$. Thus $2S=(a+b)h$, so $S=\frac{(a+b)h}{2}$. The upper and lower bases must be the two parallel sides.

Area units convert by the square of the length conversion factor: $1\text{ m}^2=100\text{ dm}^2$ and $1\text{ dm}^2=100\text{ cm}^2$. A composite figure can be split or completed into the basic figures above, and the areas then added. Also, equal perimeters do not imply equal areas: a rectangle $8$ by $2$ and a square of side $5$ both have perimeter $20$, but their areas are $16$ and $25$.

formulas.note: 长方形面积 = 长 × 宽，用 1 平方厘米的小正方形摆一摆就能看出来。
formulas.noteEn: Rectangle: area = length × width; a grid of 1 cm² squares shows exactly why.

formulas.note: 正方形面积 = 边长 × 边长，也可以写成 $a^2$（读作 a 的平方）。
formulas.noteEn: Square: area = side × side, also written a² (a squared).

formulas.note: 平行四边形面积 = 底 × 高（割补法：沿高剪开拼成长方形）。
formulas.noteEn: Parallelogram: area = base × height (cut along the height and slide the piece to form a rectangle).

formulas.note: 三角形面积 = 底 × 高 ÷ 2：两个完全一样的三角形正好拼成一个平行四边形，所以要除以 2。
formulas.noteEn: Triangle: area = base × height ÷ 2 — two identical triangles form a parallelogram, hence the division by 2.

formulas.note: 梯形面积 =（上底 + 下底）× 高 ÷ 2：两个完全一样的梯形拼成平行四边形，也要除以 2。
formulas.noteEn: Trapezoid: area = (upper base + lower base) × height ÷ 2 — again two identical trapezoids make a parallelogram.

formulas.note: 面积单位之间的进率是 100（长度单位进率才是 10）。
formulas.noteEn: Adjacent area units differ by a factor of 100 (length units differ by 10).

properties: 面积表示物体的表面或封闭图形的大小；常用单位：平方厘米、平方分米、平方米
长方形面积 = 长 × 宽；正方形面积 = 边长 × 边长
平行四边形面积 = 底 × 高（割补法：转化成长方形）；底和高必须是相对应的一组
三角形面积 = 底 × 高 ÷ 2；梯形面积 =（上底 + 下底）× 高 ÷ 2，「÷ 2」都不能丢
面积单位换算：1 平方米 = 100 平方分米，1 平方分米 = 100 平方厘米
propertiesEn: Area measures the size of a surface or a closed figure; common units: cm², dm², m²
Rectangle: area = length × width; square: area = side × side
Parallelogram: area = base × height (found by cutting and sliding it into a rectangle); base and height must match each other
Triangle: area = base × height ÷ 2; trapezoid: area = (upper base + lower base) × height ÷ 2 — never drop the ÷2
Conversions: 1 m² = 100 dm² and 1 dm² = 100 cm²

examples.problem: 一块平行四边形菜地，底是 6 米，高是 4 米。它的面积是多少平方米？
examples.solution: 平行四边形面积 = 底 × 高 = 6 × 4 = 24（平方米）。答：它的面积是 24 平方米。（高要选与这条底相对应的高）

examples.problem: 一面三角形小红旗，底是 5 分米、高是 4 分米，面积是多少平方分米？一个梯形零件，上底 3 厘米、下底 5 厘米、高 4 厘米，面积是多少平方厘米？

expression.text: S 表示面积：长方形 S = ab；平行四边形 S = ah；三角形 S = ah ÷ 2
expression.note: 同一个公式里，底 a 和它对应的高 h 要「配对」，不能拿另一条底的高来算。
expression.noteEn: In each formula the base a must pair with its own height h; do not mix a base with the height of another side.

circle-elementary.definition:
圆中心的一点叫**圆心**（通常记作 $O$），它决定圆的位置。从圆心到圆上任意一点的线段叫**半径** $r$，半径的长短决定圆的大小；通过圆心并且两端都在圆上的线段叫**直径** $d$。在同一个圆里，**直径是半径的 2 倍：$d = 2r$**。

圆的周长（绕圆一圈的长度）和直径有关系：量一量就会发现，无论圆大圆小，周长总是直径的 **3 倍多一些**。这个固定的倍数叫**圆周率**，记作 $\pi$。$\pi$ 是一个**无限不循环小数**（$\pi = 3.1415926\ldots$），计算时通常取 $\pi \approx 3.14$。所以**圆的周长 $C = \pi d = 2\pi r$**。

把圆平均分成很多个小扇形再拼起来，可以拼成一个近似的长方形：长是圆周长的一半 $\pi r$，宽是半径 $r$，所以**圆的面积 $S = \pi r^2$**。注意 $r^2$ 是「半径乘半径」，不是「半径乘 2」！另外还有：圆环面积 $= \pi (R^2 - r^2)$；扇形面积 $= \frac{n}{360} \times \pi r^2$（$n$ 是圆心角的度数）。算**半圆的周长**时千万别忘了加上直径：半圆周长 $= \pi r + 2r$。
circle-elementary.definitionEn:
The point at the centre of a circle is the **centre**, usually written $O$, and it fixes where the circle lies. A segment from the centre to any point on the circle is a **radius** $r$, and its length fixes how big the circle is. A segment that passes through the centre with both ends on the circle is a **diameter** $d$. In the same circle the diameter is twice the radius: $d = 2r$.

Measure around any circle and you find that the circumference is always a little more than 3 diameters — big circle or small. This fixed ratio is called **π (pi)**. It is an **infinite non-repeating decimal** ($\pi = 3.1415926\ldots$), and we usually take $\pi \approx 3.14$. Hence **$C = \pi d = 2\pi r$**.

Cut a circle into many small sectors and rearrange them, and they almost form a rectangle: its length is half the circumference $\pi r$ and its width is the radius $r$. So **$S = \pi r^2$** — remember, $r^2$ means $r \times r$, not $2r$! Two more to know: the area of a ring is $\pi (R^2 - r^2)$, and the area of a sector is $\frac{n}{360}\pi r^2$, where $n$ is the central angle in degrees. For the **perimeter of a semicircle**, do not forget the diameter: $\pi r + 2r$.
derivation: 圆是平面上到定点 $O$（圆心）的距离等于定长 $r$（半径）的所有点组成的图形。圆心决定圆的位置，半径决定圆的大小。通过圆心并且两端都在圆上的线段是直径 $d$；在同一个圆中 $d=2r$，即 $r=\frac{d}{2}$。
任意圆的周长 $C$ 与直径 $d$ 的比值是一个常数，记作 $\pi$。测量表明周长总是直径的 $3$ 倍多，且 $\pi=3.1415926\ldots$ 是无限不循环小数，计算时常取 $3.14$。由 $\frac{C}{d}=\pi$ 得 $C=\pi d=2\pi r$。$\pi$ 是一个比值，没有单位；周长的单位与半径相同。
把圆平均分成 $n$ 个全等的小扇形，再交替拼成一个近似长方形：长约为圆周长的一半 $\pi r$，宽为半径 $r$。拼成图形的面积始终等于圆的面积；$n$ 越大，它的形状越接近长为 $\pi r$、宽为 $r$ 的长方形，因此圆面积等于该长方形面积 $\pi r^2$。因此 $S_{\text{圆}}=\pi r^2$。注意 $r^2=r\times r$，不是 $2r$。
半径 $r=3$ 厘米时，$C=2\pi r=2\times3.14\times3=18.84$ 厘米；$S=\pi r^2=3.14\times3^2=3.14\times9=28.26$ 平方厘米。两个结果的单位不同，不能比较数值大小。若题目给出的是直径 $d$，要先求 $r=\frac{d}{2}$，再算面积。
半圆的弧长是圆周长的一半 $\pi r$，但半圆图形的周长还要加上一条直径 $2r$，所以 $C_{\text{半圆}}=\pi r+2r$；面积是圆面积的一半，$S=\frac{1}{2}\pi r^2$。例：直径 $8$ 米，则 $r=4$ 米，周长 $=3.14\times4+8=20.56$ 米，面积 $=3.14\times16\div2=25.12$ 平方米。
圆环由半径为 $R$ 的外圆挖去同心的半径为 $r$ 的内圆得到，其中 $R>r$，面积 $S=\pi R^2-\pi r^2=\pi(R^2-r^2)$。圆心角为 $n^\circ$ 的扇形占整个圆的 $\frac{n}{360}$，所以 $S=\frac{n}{360}\pi r^2$，其中 $0\le n\le360$；它的弧长为 $\frac{n}{360}\cdot2\pi r$。
derivationEn: A circle is the set of all points in the plane at a fixed distance $r$ (the radius) from a fixed point $O$ (the centre). The centre fixes the position of the circle and the radius fixes its size. A segment through the centre with both ends on the circle is a diameter $d$; in the same circle $d=2r$, that is, $r=\frac{d}{2}$.

For every circle the ratio of the circumference $C$ to the diameter $d$ is a constant denoted $\pi$. Measurements show that the circumference is always a little more than $3$ diameters, and $\pi=3.1415926\ldots$ is an infinite non-repeating decimal, usually taken as $3.14$ in calculations. From $\frac{C}{d}=\pi$ we get $C=\pi d=2\pi r$. The number $\pi$ is a ratio and has no unit; the circumference has the same unit as the radius.

Divide a circle into $n$ congruent small sectors and rearrange them alternately into an approximate rectangle whose length is half the circumference $\pi r$ and whose width is the radius $r$. The rearranged figure always has exactly the circle's area; as $n$ grows, its shape approaches a rectangle of length $\pi r$ and width $r$, so the circle's area equals $\pi r^2$. Hence $S_{\text{circle}}=\pi r^2$. Note that $r^2=r\times r$, not $2r$.

For radius $r=3$ cm, $C=2\pi r=2\times3.14\times3=18.84$ cm and $S=\pi r^2=3.14\times3^2=3.14\times9=28.26\text{ cm}^2$. The two results have different units, so their numerical values cannot be compared. If the diameter $d$ is given, first find $r=\frac{d}{2}$ and then compute the area.

The arc of a semicircle has length equal to half the circumference, $\pi r$, but the perimeter of the semicircular figure also includes the diameter $2r$, so $C_{\text{semicircle}}=\pi r+2r$. Its area is half the circle's area, $S=\frac{1}{2}\pi r^2$. Example: with diameter $8$ m, $r=4$ m, the perimeter is $3.14\times4+8=20.56$ m and the area is $3.14\times16\div2=25.12\text{ m}^2$.

A ring is obtained by removing a concentric inner circle of radius $r$ from an outer circle of radius $R$, where $R>r$; its area is $S=\pi R^2-\pi r^2=\pi(R^2-r^2)$. A sector with central angle $n^\circ$ occupies the fraction $\frac{n}{360}$ of the whole circle, so $S=\frac{n}{360}\pi r^2$ with $0\le n\le360$; its arc length is $\frac{n}{360}\cdot2\pi r$.

formulas.note: 在同一个圆里，直径是半径的 2 倍；半径是直径的一半。
formulas.noteEn: In the same circle the diameter is twice the radius, and the radius is half the diameter.

formulas.note: 圆的周长 = 圆周率 × 直径 = 2 × 圆周率 × 半径；计算时取 $\pi \approx 3.14$。
formulas.noteEn: Circumference = π × diameter = 2πr, with π ≈ 3.14 in calculations.

formulas.note: 圆的面积 = 圆周率 × 半径 × 半径。$r^2$ 是半径的平方，不是半径乘 2。
formulas.noteEn: Area = π × r × r. Here r² is the radius squared, not 2 × r.

formulas.note: 圆环面积 = 外圆面积 − 内圆面积；$R$ 是大圆半径，$r$ 是小圆半径。
formulas.noteEn: Ring: area = outer circle − inner circle, where R is the outer radius and r the inner radius.

formulas.note: 扇形面积 = 圆心角 $n$ 占 360° 的几分之几，就占圆面积的几分之几。
formulas.noteEn: Sector: the area is the same fraction of the circle's area as n° is of 360°.

formulas.note: 半圆的周长 = 圆周长的一半 + 一条直径（最容易漏掉直径！）。

solid-volume-elementary.definition:
物体所占空间的大小叫**体积**。把长方体切成棱长 1 厘米的小正方体：每行摆「长」个、摆「宽」行、叠「高」层，一共能摆 长 × 宽 × 高 个，所以**长方体的体积 = 长 × 宽 × 高 = 底面积 × 高**。正方体是特殊的长方体，**正方体的体积 = 棱长 × 棱长 × 棱长 = 棱长³**（不是 3 × 棱长！）。

把圆柱切成许多小块，也能拼成一个近似的长方体：底面积是 $\pi r^2$，高是 $h$，所以**圆柱的体积 = 底面积 × 高 = $\pi r^2 h$**。圆锥最有意思：等底等高时，用装满沙子的圆锥往圆柱里倒，正好倒 **3 次**才装满——所以**圆锥的体积是圆柱的 $\frac{1}{3}$**，即 $V = \frac{1}{3} \times$ 底面积 × 高 $= \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$。这个 $\frac{1}{3}$ 最容易被忘掉！

求**表面积**就是求所有面的面积之和：长方体表面积 =（长×宽 + 长×高 + 宽×高）× 2；正方体表面积 = 棱长² × 6；圆柱的侧面展开是一个长方形，侧面积 = 底面周长 × 高 = $2\pi rh$，再加上两个底面，圆柱表面积 = $2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2$。体积单位有立方厘米、立方分米、立方米：**1 立方米 = 1000 立方分米，1 立方分米 = 1000 立方厘米**；其中 1 立方分米就是 1 升。
solid-volume-elementary.definitionEn:
The **volume** of a solid is how much space it takes up. Slice a cuboid into 1 cm cubes: 「length」 cubes per row, 「width」 rows and 「height」 layers, so you need length × width × height cubes. Hence **volume of a cuboid = length × width × height = base area × height**. A cube is a special cuboid, so **volume of a cube = edge × edge × edge = edge³** (not 3 × edge!).

Slice a cylinder into many pieces and they rearrange into an approximate cuboid, with base area $\pi r^2$ and height $h$, so **volume of a cylinder = base area × height = $\pi r^2 h$**. A cone is the most surprising: with equal base and equal height, you must pour a full cone of sand into the cylinder exactly **3 times** to fill it — so **a cone is $\frac{1}{3}$ of the cylinder**, i.e. $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$. That $\frac{1}{3}$ is the most commonly forgotten factor!

A **surface area** is the sum of the areas of all the faces: cuboid = (length×width + length×height + width×height) × 2; cube = edge² × 6. The side of a cylinder unrolls into a rectangle, so its lateral area = base circumference × height = $2\pi rh$, and adding the two bases gives $2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2$. Volume units: **1 m³ = 1000 dm³, 1 dm³ = 1000 cm³**, and 1 dm³ is exactly 1 litre.
derivation: 物体所占空间的大小叫做体积，用立方厘米、立方分米、立方米等体积单位度量。容器内部能容纳物体的体积叫做容积，常用升（L）、毫升（mL）：$1\text{ L}=1\text{ dm}^3$，$1\text{ mL}=1\text{ cm}^3$。体积从外面度量物体占的空间，容积从里面度量容器能装多少；体积单位与容积单位可以换算（$1\text{ L}=1\text{ dm}^3$，$1\text{ mL}=1\text{ cm}^3$），但同一容器的体积一般大于容积，不能把二者直接等同。

设 $a,b,h$ 为正整数（以 $1$ 为单位），把长方体划分成棱长为 $1$ 的单位小正方体：每行 $a$ 个，有 $b$ 行，共 $h$ 层，所以总数为 $a\times b\times h$。因此 $V_{\text{长方体}}=abh$。由于底面积是 $ab$，也可以写成 $V=S_{\text{底}}h$。当 $a=b=h$ 时得到正方体，$V=a^3$；这里 $a^3=a\cdot a\cdot a$，不是 $3a$。
把圆柱的底面分成许多相等的扇形，再沿高切开，可以拼成一个近似长方体：底面积仍为 $\pi r^2$，高为 $h$，所以 $V_{\text{圆柱}}=\pi r^2h$。分割越细，拼成的立体越接近长方体。这个公式适用于直圆柱，其中 $r$ 是底面半径，$h$ 是两底面之间的垂直距离。
等底等高时，圆锥的体积是圆柱的 $\frac{1}{3}$：用装满沙子的圆锥向圆柱里倒，倒 $3$ 次恰好装满，所以 $3V_{\text{锥}}=V_{\text{柱}}=\pi r^2h$，即 $V_{\text{锥}}=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2h$。条件「等底等高」不能省略；若底面积或高不同，必须分别计算，不能直接取三分之一。
表面积是所有面的面积之和，单位是平方单位，与体积的立方单位不同。长方体 $S=2(ab+ah+bh)$；正方体 $S=6a^2$；圆柱 $S=2\pi rh+2\pi r^2$，其中侧面展开成长方形，还要加上两个底面。例：长 $5$、宽 $3$、高 $4$ 厘米的长方体，$V=60$ 立方厘米，$S=2(15+20+12)=94$ 平方厘米。

体积单位之间的进率是长度单位进率的立方：$1\text{ m}^3=1000\text{ dm}^3$，$1\text{ dm}^3=1000\text{ cm}^3$，所以 $1\text{ m}^3=10^6\text{ cm}^3$。例：底面半径 $2$ 厘米、高 $6$ 厘米的圆柱与它等底等高的圆锥，$V_{\text{柱}}=3.14\times4\times6=75.36$ 立方厘米，$V_{\text{锥}}=75.36\div3=25.12$ 立方厘米。容积换算时 $1\text{ L}=1\text{ dm}^3=1000\text{ mL}$。
derivationEn: The volume of a solid is the amount of space it occupies, measured in cubic centimetres, cubic decimetres, cubic metres and similar units. The capacity of a container is the volume it can hold inside, commonly measured in litres (L) and millilitres (mL): $1\text{ L}=1\text{ dm}^3$ and $1\text{ mL}=1\text{ cm}^3$. Volume measures the space occupied from outside, while capacity measures how much a container holds from inside; their units convert ($1\text{ L}=1\text{ dm}^3$, $1\text{ mL}=1\text{ cm}^3$), but a container's volume is generally greater than its capacity, so the two quantities are not interchangeable.

Assume $a,b,h$ are positive integers in the chosen unit; divide the cuboid into unit cubes of edge $1$: each row has $a$ cubes, there are $b$ rows and $h$ layers, so the total number is $a\times b\times h$. Hence $V_{\text{cuboid}}=abh$. Since the base area is $ab$, this can also be written $V=S_{\text{base}}h$. When $a=b=h$ the solid is a cube and $V=a^3$; here $a^3=a\cdot a\cdot a$, not $3a$.

Divide the base of a cylinder into many equal sectors and cut along a height; the pieces rearrange into an approximate cuboid with base area $\pi r^2$ and height $h$. Therefore $V_{\text{cylinder}}=\pi r^2h$. The finer the division, the closer the solid is to a cuboid. This formula applies to a right cylinder, where $r$ is the base radius and $h$ is the perpendicular distance between the two bases.

When a cone and a cylinder have equal bases and equal heights, the cone's volume is $\frac{1}{3}$ of the cylinder's: filling the cylinder with sand using the cone takes exactly $3$ cone-loads, so $3V_{\text{cone}}=V_{\text{cylinder}}=\pi r^2h$, hence $V_{\text{cone}}=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2h$. The condition 'equal bases and equal heights' cannot be omitted; if either differs, compute separately rather than taking one third.

Surface area is the sum of the areas of all faces, measured in square units, which differ from the cubic units of volume. For a cuboid $S=2(ab+ah+bh)$; for a cube $S=6a^2$; for a cylinder $S=2\pi rh+2\pi r^2$, where the lateral surface unrolls to a rectangle and the two bases are added. Example: a cuboid $5$ by $3$ by $4$ cm has $V=60\text{ cm}^3$ and $S=2(15+20+12)=94\text{ cm}^2$.

Volume units convert by the cube of the length conversion factor: $1\text{ m}^3=1000\text{ dm}^3$, $1\text{ dm}^3=1000\text{ cm}^3$, so $1\text{ m}^3=10^6\text{ cm}^3$. Example: a cylinder of base radius $2$ cm and height $6$ cm, together with a cone of the same base and height, has $V_{\text{cylinder}}=3.14\times4\times6=75.36\text{ cm}^3$ and $V_{\text{cone}}=75.36\div3=25.12\text{ cm}^3$. For capacity, $1\text{ L}=1\text{ dm}^3=1000\text{ mL}$.

figures-motion-elementary.definition:
长方形、正方形、圆这些图形，除了安安静静地「待」在那里，还能在平面上**动起来**。小学里最常见的三种运动是：**平移**、**旋转**和**轴对称**。它们有一个共同点：动过之后，图形的**形状和大小都不变**，改变的只是位置或方向。

把图形沿着一条直线移动，叫做**平移**。说平移，必须说清两件事：往哪个**方向**移、一共移了多**远**（距离）。比如电梯载着人笔直地上升，就是在做平移；小汽车在笔直的马路上向前开 10 米，车身的图形也平移了 10 米。平移**只改变位置，不改变形状和大小**：平移前后两个图形一模一样，能完全重合；每个点都朝同一个方向移动同样远，所以对应点之间的连线互相平行、并且一样长。

图形绕着一个点（或一条轴）转动，叫做**旋转**。说旋转，要说清三件事：绕哪个点转（**旋转中心**）、往哪个方向转（**顺时针**或**逆时针**）、转了多少度（**角度**）。例如「钟面上的一根指针绕中心顺时针旋转 90°」。旋转前后，图形的形状和大小也**不改变**，只是转了方向。

如果一个图形沿着一条直线对折，直线两边的部分能**完全重合**，这个图形就是**轴对称图形**，这条直线叫做它的**对称轴**。常见图形的对称轴条数要记牢：长方形 **2 条**，正方形 **4 条**，等腰三角形 **1 条**，等边三角形 **3 条**，圆有**无数条**。
figures-motion-elementary.definitionEn:
Rectangles, squares and circles do not just sit still—they can **move** in the plane. The three movements met in primary school are **translation**, **rotation** and **axial symmetry**. They share one feature: after the movement the **shape and size of the figure do not change**; only its position or direction does.

Sliding a figure along a straight line is a **translation**. To describe one, you must say two things: in which **direction** it moves and how **far** it goes. A lift carrying people straight up is translating; a car driving 10 metres along a straight road translates the car's shape by 10 metres. A translation **changes only the position, never the shape or size**: the figure and its image fit exactly on top of each other, and the segments joining corresponding points are parallel and equal.

Turning a figure about a point (or an axis) is a **rotation**. To describe one, say three things: about which point (the **centre of rotation**), in which direction (**clockwise** or **anticlockwise**), and through what **angle**—for example, 'a clock hand rotates 90° clockwise about the centre'. A rotation also leaves the shape and size unchanged; only the direction turns.

If a figure can be folded along a straight line so that the two parts **coincide exactly**, it is **axially symmetric**, and that line is called its **axis of symmetry**. Remember the numbers of axes: a rectangle has **2**, a square **4**, an isosceles triangle **1**, an equilateral triangle **3**, and a circle has **infinitely many**.
derivation: 平移、旋转和轴对称都是平面图形的变换。三者的共同点是：变换前后两个图形全等，即对应边相等、对应角相等，形状和大小都不改变；改变的只是位置或方向。因此可以用对应点、对应边来描述变换前后的关系。
平移由方向（平移向量）和距离完全确定。图形上每一点都沿同一方向移动同样的距离；对应点之间的连线互相平行（或在同一直线上）且长度相等，对应边也平行且相等。平移不改变图形的方向。例：小车沿直路前进 $10$ 米，车身上每一点都平移了 $10$ 米。
旋转由旋转中心 $O$、方向（顺时针或逆时针）和角度 $\theta$ 确定。图形上每一点都绕 $O$ 转过同样的角 $\theta$，对应点到 $O$ 的距离保持不变。旋转不改变形状和大小，但会改变方向；当 $\theta=360^\circ$ 时图形回到原来的位置。描述旋转时，中心、方向、角度三个要素缺一不可。
如果沿直线 $l$ 对折后，图形在 $l$ 两侧的部分完全重合，那么这个图形是轴对称图形，$l$ 是它的对称轴。此时每一对对应点的连线都被 $l$ 垂直平分；对应线段相等，对应角相等。轴对称会改变图形的方向（左右翻转），所以一般不能由平移或旋转得到。
常见图形的对称轴条数：线段有 $2$ 条（垂直平分线以及它所在的直线），长方形有 $2$ 条，正方形有 $4$ 条，等腰三角形有 $1$ 条，等边三角形有 $3$ 条，圆有无数条（每条直径所在的直线都是对称轴）。一般的平行四边形（非矩形、非菱形）没有对称轴。
判断变换要看对应关系，不能只看位置：对应点连线平行、同向且等长（各点位移向量相同），才是平移；对应点绕同一点按同一方向转过相同角度，才是旋转；对应点连线被同一直线垂直平分，是轴对称。例：方格纸上点 $A$ 向右平移 $4$ 格、向上平移 $2$ 格，每一个对应点都作同样的移动，图形形状和大小不变。
derivationEn: Translation, rotation and axial symmetry are transformations of plane figures. They share one property: the figure and its image are congruent, so corresponding sides and corresponding angles are equal, and neither shape nor size changes; only position or orientation changes. Corresponding points and corresponding sides can therefore be used to describe the relation between the figure and its image.

A translation is completely determined by a direction (translation vector) and a distance. Every point of the figure moves the same distance in the same direction; segments joining corresponding points are parallel (or collinear) and equal, and corresponding sides are parallel and equal. A translation does not change the orientation of the figure. Example: a car moving $10$ m along a straight road translates every point of its body by $10$ m.

A rotation is determined by its centre $O$, its direction (clockwise or anticlockwise) and its angle $\theta$. Every point of the figure turns through the same angle $\theta$ about $O$, and each corresponding point keeps its distance from $O$. Rotation preserves shape and size but changes orientation; when $\theta=360^\circ$ the figure returns to its original position. Centre, direction and angle are all needed to describe a rotation.

If a figure can be folded along a line $l$ so that the two parts on opposite sides of $l$ coincide exactly, then the figure is axially symmetric and $l$ is an axis of symmetry. Every segment joining a pair of corresponding points is perpendicularly bisected by $l$; corresponding segments and corresponding angles are equal. Axial symmetry reverses orientation (a left-right flip), so in general it cannot be produced by a translation or a rotation.

Numbers of axes of symmetry for common figures: a line segment has $2$ (its perpendicular bisector and the line containing it), a rectangle has $2$, a square has $4$, an isosceles triangle has $1$, an equilateral triangle has $3$, and a circle has infinitely many (every line through a diameter is an axis). A general parallelogram that is neither a rectangle nor a rhombus has no axis of symmetry.

To identify a transformation, examine corresponding points rather than position alone: if the segments joining corresponding points are parallel, codirected and equal (the same displacement vector), the transformation is a translation; if corresponding points turn about the same point in the same direction through the same angle, it is a rotation; if the joining segments are perpendicularly bisected by one line, it is axial symmetry. Example: on squared paper, move point $A$ $4$ squares right and $2$ squares up; every corresponding point makes the same move, so shape and size are unchanged.

formulas.latex: \text{平移：只改变位置，不改变形状和大小}
formulas.note: 平移由**方向**和**距离**决定；对应点之间的连线互相平行，并且一样长。
formulas.noteEn: A translation is fixed by a **direction** and a **distance**; the segments joining corresponding points are parallel and equal.

formulas.latex: \text{旋转：绕一个点转动（中心、方向、角度）}
formulas.note: 说清绕哪个点（旋转中心）、顺时针还是逆时针、转了多少度；旋转后形状和大小不变。
formulas.noteEn: State the centre of rotation, the direction (clockwise or anticlockwise) and the angle; the shape and size stay the same.

formulas.latex: \text{轴对称：沿一条直线对折，两边完全重合}
formulas.note: 对折后两边能完全重合的图形叫轴对称图形，折痕所在的直线叫对称轴。
formulas.noteEn: A figure whose two halves coincide when folded along a line is axially symmetric; the crease is its axis of symmetry.

formulas.latex: \text{对称轴条数：长方形 }2,\ \text{正方形 }4,\ \text{等腰三角形 }1,\ \text{等边三角形 }3,\ \text{圆无数条}
formulas.note: 这是常见考点，最好动手折一折、数一数，再记牢。
formulas.noteEn: A classic test point: fold the shapes and count, then memorise the numbers.

properties: 平移只改变图形的位置，不改变形状和大小；说清方向和距离，平移就确定了。
旋转只改变图形的方向（位置也可能改变），形状和大小不变；描述旋转要说出中心、方向和角度。
轴对称图形沿对称轴对折后，两边能完全重合；对称轴两边的图形形状相同、大小相等。
长方形有 2 条对称轴，正方形有 4 条，等腰三角形有 1 条，等边三角形有 3 条，圆有无数条对称轴。
生活中的例子：电梯上下运行是平移，钟表指针的转动是旋转，蝴蝶的左右两只翅膀关于身体中线成轴对称。
propertiesEn: A translation changes only the position of a figure, not its shape or size; a direction and a distance determine it completely.
A rotation changes the direction (and possibly the position) of a figure but keeps its shape and size; describe it by centre, direction and angle.
Folding an axially symmetric figure along its axis makes the two halves coincide exactly; the two sides have the same shape and size.
A rectangle has 2 axes of symmetry, a square 4, an isosceles triangle 1, an equilateral triangle 3, and a circle infinitely many.
Everyday examples: a lift moving up and down is a translation, a clock hand turning is a rotation, and a butterfly's wings are axially symmetric about its centre line.

examples.problem: 下面三种现象各属于哪种运动？① 电梯笔直地上升；② 钟表的指针转动；③ 蝴蝶的左右两只翅膀。
examples.solution: ① 电梯沿直线向上移动，是**平移**：只改变位置，形状和大小不变，方向是「向上」，距离就是上升的高度。② 指针绕着中心转动，是**旋转**：旋转中心是表盘的中心，方向是顺时针。③ 蝴蝶的左右翅膀沿身体中间的那条线对折后能完全重合，是**轴对称**，这条线就是对称轴。

examples.problem: 填一填常见图形的对称轴条数：长方形（ ）条，正方形（ ）条，等腰三角形（ ）条，等边三角形（ ）条，圆（ ）条。
examples.solution: 长方形 **2 条**（两条对边中点连线所在的直线）；正方形 **4 条**（两条对边中点连线所在的直线，再加上两条对角线所在的直线）；等腰三角形 **1 条**（底边上的高所在的直线）；等边三角形 **3 条**（每条边的中点与对顶点的连线所在的直线）；圆有**无数条**（每条直径所在的直线都是它的对称轴）。

observing-objects.definition:
站在物体的前面看一看，走到它的上面看一看，再跑到它的侧面看一看，你看到的形状往往不一样。所以观察物体时，一定要先说清**从哪个方向看**，别人才能知道你说的是哪一种样子。

小学里主要从三个方向观察：从**前面（正面）**看、从**上面**看、从**左面（侧面）**看。把每个方向看到的形状分别画下来，就得到「从三个方向看到的图形」。同一个物体，从不同方向看到的形状**可能不同**：一个长方体盒子，从前面看是一个长方形，从上面看是另一个长方形，从左面看又是大小不同的长方形。当然也可能**相同**：正方体从前面、上面、左面看，都是正方形。

特别要注意：只根据**一个**方向看到的图形，**不能确定**物体的形状。比如从前面看到的是一个正方形，这个物体可能是正方体，也可能是一个「前面看是正方形、其实很薄」的方盒子，还可能是别的立体图形；只有结合从上面、从左面看到的图形，才能确定它到底长什么样。

「搭积木」也要用这个本领：用同样的小正方体搭出符合要求的立体图形。可以**先照从上面看到的形状摆好「占地」的位置**，再**按从前面、左面看到的形状一层层往上加高**，就能搭出正确的图形。观察时眼睛要正对着物体看（视线与观察的那个面垂直），才不容易看错形状。
observing-objects.definitionEn:
Stand in front of an object, then above it, then to its side: the shapes you see are often different. That is why, when observing an object, you must say **from which direction** you are looking.

In primary school we observe from three directions: from the **front**, from **above** and from the **left**. Drawing the shape seen from each direction gives the 'three views'. The same object may look **different** from different directions—a cuboid is one rectangle from the front, another from above and a third from the left—or **the same**: a cube looks like a square from all three directions.

One important warning: the shape seen from **a single** direction **cannot determine** the object. A square seen from the front may come from a cube, from a very thin box whose front face is a square, or from other solids; only the views from above and from the left settle the question.

Building with unit cubes uses the same skill: **place the cubes according to the view from above (the 'footprint'), then add layers according to the views from the front and from the left**. Keep your line of sight perpendicular to the face you are observing, so the shape is not distorted.
derivation: 观察物体时要说明观察方向。小学通常从前面（正面）、上面、左面三个方向观察，视线分别垂直于对应的面，得到的是正投影视图：从前面看到长 $\times$ 高，从上面看到长 $\times$ 宽，从左面看到宽 $\times$ 高。方向不同，看到的形状可能不同。
长方体长 $6$、宽 $4$、高 $2$（单位：厘米）：从前面看是 $6\times2$ 的长方形，从上面看是 $6\times4$ 的长方形，从左面看是 $4\times2$ 的长方形。三个视图的边由不同的两条棱决定，所以大小一般不同；只有当相应的两条棱相等时，两个视图才可能相同。
正方体棱长为 $a$，从前面、上面、左面看到的都是边长为 $a$ 的正方形，三个视图完全相同。反过来，若一个长方体在三个方向上的视图都是同样大小的正方形，则它的长、宽、高都等于 $a$，这个长方体就是正方体。但视图相同并不意味着物体内部结构相同。

只看一个方向不能确定物体的形状。例：$3\times3\times3$ 的正方体与 $3\times1\times3$ 的长方体（长 $3$、宽 $1$、高 $3$，把 $3\times3$ 的面朝前），从前面看都是 $3\times3$ 的正方形；但从上面看分别是 $3\times3$ 与 $3\times1$ 的长方形，从左面看分别是 $3\times3$ 与 $1\times3$ 的长方形。因此必须结合多个方向的视图。
用小正方体搭立体图形时，从上面看到的图形给出「占地」位置，即哪几格有方块；从前面看到的图形给出每一列的最大高度；从左面看到的图形给出每一行的最大高度。先按俯视图摆好位置，再用正视图和左视图确定各位置高度的上限（每列、每行的最大值），据此选择一种满足所有最大值的摆法；搭法不一定唯一。

三个视图能提供很强的限制，但不一定能唯一确定物体。例：俯视图是 $2\times2$ 的四个方格，正视图两列的高度都为 $2$，左视图两行的高度都为 $2$；高度矩阵 $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$ 与 $\begin{pmatrix}2&2\\2&1\end{pmatrix}$ 都满足这些视图，却是不同的搭法。因此读图时还要说明是否允许隐藏结构，并检查所有视图是否同时满足。
derivationEn: When observing an object, state the direction of view. Primary school usually uses three directions: from the front, from above and from the left, with the line of sight perpendicular to the corresponding face. These are orthographic views: from the front one sees length $\times$ height, from above length $\times$ width, and from the left width $\times$ height. Different directions may give different shapes.

A cuboid of length $6$, width $4$ and height $2$ (in centimetres) looks like a $6\times2$ rectangle from the front, a $6\times4$ rectangle from above, and a $4\times2$ rectangle from the left. The sides of the three views are determined by different pairs of edges, so their sizes generally differ; two views can coincide only when the corresponding pair of edges are equal.

For a cube of edge $a$, the views from the front, from above and from the left are all squares of side $a$, so the three views are identical. Conversely, if a cuboid has square views of the same size in all three directions, then its length, width and height all equal $a$, so the cuboid is a cube. Identical views, however, do not imply identical internal structure.

A single view cannot determine the shape of an object. Example: a $3\times3\times3$ cube and a $3\times1\times3$ cuboid (length $3$, width $1$, height $3$, with a $3\times3$ face at the front) both look like a $3\times3$ square from the front; from above they look like $3\times3$ and $3\times1$ rectangles respectively, and from the left like $3\times3$ and $1\times3$ rectangles. Several directions must therefore be combined.

When building with unit cubes, the view from above gives the footprint, that is, which grid positions contain cubes; the view from the front gives the maximum height of each column; the view from the left gives the maximum height of each row. Place the cubes according to the top view first, then use the front and left views to bound the height at each position (column/row maxima), and choose one assignment satisfying all maxima; the solid need not be unique.

Three views impose strong constraints but need not determine the solid uniquely. Example: the top view is a full $2\times2$ block of four squares, the front view has height $2$ in both columns, and the left view has height $2$ in both rows. The height matrices $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$ and $\begin{pmatrix}2&2\\2&1\end{pmatrix}$ both satisfy these views but describe different arrangements. When reading views, one must therefore state whether hidden structure is allowed and check that all views hold simultaneously.

formulas.latex: \text{观察方向：从前面（正面）、从上面、从左面（侧面）}
formulas.note: 从三个方向观察同一个物体；看到的形状常常不同，也可能相同（例如正方体）。
formulas.noteEn: Observe one object from three directions; the shapes are often different, though they may coincide (as for a cube).

formulas.latex: \text{只看一个方向} \Rightarrow \text{不能确定物体的形状}
formulas.note: 例如从前面看是正方形，物体可能是正方体，也可能是很薄的长方体；要综合几个方向才能确定。
formulas.noteEn: For instance a square seen from the front may come from a cube or from a thin cuboid; several views together are needed.

formulas.latex: \text{从前面看：长}\times\text{高},\quad \text{从上面看：长}\times\text{宽},\quad \text{从左面看：宽}\times\text{高}
formulas.note: 以长方体为例：三个方向看到的长方形由不同的两条棱决定，所以大小通常不一样。
formulas.noteEn: For a cuboid the three rectangles are fixed by different pairs of edges (length, width, height), so their sizes usually differ.

properties: 从前面（正面）、上面、左面三个方向观察同一个物体，看到的形状可能不同。
只根据一个方向看到的图形，不能确定物体的形状；要看多个方向（通常三个方向）才行。
不同方向看到的形状有时也会相同，例如正方体从前面、上面、左面看都是正方形。
用同样的小正方体搭图形：先照从上面看到的形状摆好位置，再按从前面、左面看到的样子确定每一处的高度。
观察时眼睛要正对物体，视线与要观察的那个面垂直，看到的形状才不会变形。
propertiesEn: Looking at the same object from the front, from above and from the left may give different shapes.
One direction alone cannot determine the shape of an object; several views (usually three) are needed.
The views sometimes coincide—a cube looks like a square from the front, from above and from the left.
When building with unit cubes: first place them according to the view from above, then fix the height of every position using the front and left views.
Keep your eyes straight in front of the object, with the line of sight perpendicular to the face, so the shape is not distorted.

examples.problem: 一个长方体木块，长 6 厘米、宽 4 厘米、高 2 厘米。从前面、上面、左面看，各看到什么形状？（说清边长）
examples.solution: 从前面看：长 6 厘米、高 2 厘米的长方形；从上面看：长 6 厘米、宽 4 厘米的长方形；从左面看：宽 4 厘米、高 2 厘米的长方形。三个方向看到的都是长方形，但大小不同，所以观察时一定要说清方向。

examples.problem: 小丽从前面看一个物体，看到的是一个正方形。她说：「这个物体一定是正方体。」她说的对吗？为什么？
examples.solution: 不对。从**一个**方向看到的图形**不能确定**物体的形状：从前面看是正方形，它可能是一个正方体，也可能是一个「前面是正方形、但很薄」的长方体盒子，还可能是别的立体图形。要多看几个方向——比如再从上面、从左面看——才能确定它到底是什么样子。

statistics-charts.definition:
收集来的数据像一堆散乱的珠子，把它画成**统计图**就一眼看明白了。小学常用的统计图有三种：**条形统计图**、**折线统计图**和**扇形统计图**。其中**条形统计图**用直条的**长短**表示数量的多少：直条越长，数量越多。它最大的优点是能**清楚地看出数量的多少**，比较谁多谁少最方便。

**折线统计图**把每个数据用一个点标出来，再用线段顺次连起来。它不但能看出数量的多少，还能**清楚地看出数量增减变化的趋势**：折线往上走，说明数量在增加；往下走，说明数量在减少。记录气温、身高等随时间变化的数据，用折线统计图最合适。

**扇形统计图**把整个圆看成总数（100%），每一个扇形表示一部分。它能**清楚地反映出各部分数量与总数之间的关系**，也就是各部分占总数的百分之几；所有扇形的百分比加起来，正好是 100%。

统计图还分**单式**和**复式**：只画一组数据的是单式统计图；把两组或几组数据画在一张图里的是复式统计图，便于比较。画统计图的一般步骤是：**收集数据 → 整理数据 → 制成统计表 → 画出统计图**；画好后别忘了写标题、标出数量和单位。
statistics-charts.definitionEn:
Data collected look like scattered beads; once drawn as a **statistical chart** they are clear at a glance. Primary school uses three charts by shape: the **bar chart**, the **line chart** and the **pie chart**. A **bar chart** uses the **length** of the bars for amounts: the longer the bar, the larger the amount. Its great strength is showing **how much**—comparing amounts is easiest with bars.

A **line chart** marks every value with a point and joins the points in order with segments. It shows not only how much, but also **the trend of increase and decrease**: a rising line means the amount is growing, a falling line means it is shrinking. For data that change over time, such as temperature or height, a line chart fits best.

A **pie chart** takes the whole circle as the total (100%), each sector standing for one part. It shows **the relation between each part and the whole**—what percentage of the total each part takes; all sectors add up to exactly 100%.

Charts also come in **single** and **multiple** forms: a single chart shows one set of data, while a multiple chart puts two or more sets into one picture for easy comparison. The usual steps: **collect the data, sort the data, make a table, draw the chart**—and do not forget the title, the numbers and the unit.
derivation: 统计图把整理后的数据画成图形，便于读取、比较和分析。读图前先看标题、横轴与纵轴分别表示什么、单位是什么、每一格代表多少；同一组数据用不同统计图表达时，强调的信息不同。小学常见的统计图有条形统计图、折线统计图和扇形统计图。
条形统计图用直条的长度表示数量的多少，直条越长表示数量越大。比较数量时，各直条必须从同一基线（通常为 $0$）量起，否则长度差会被夸大；读数时用「格数 $\times$ 每格代表的单位数」，不能直接把格数当作数量。复式条形统计图把两组或多组直条并列画出，便于比较。
折线统计图把数据点按时间顺序用线段连接：线段上升表示数量增加，下降表示数量减少；在横轴时间间隔相同的前提下，线段越陡，变化越快。它适合观察变化趋势，但相邻数据点之间的连线只是示意，不能据此断定两个时刻之间的实际数值；要读准确值必须看数据点或统计表。
扇形统计图把总数看作整个圆，即 $100\%$，每个扇形表示一部分。若某部分的数量为 $m$、总数为 $N$（$N>0$），则它占总数的百分比为 $\frac{m}{N}\times100\%$，对应扇形的圆心角为 $360^\circ\times\frac{m}{N}$。所有部分的百分比之和为 $100\%$，圆心角之和为 $360^\circ$；已知百分比求数量时还必须知道总数。
选择统计图要看目的：比较各类数量的多少，用条形统计图；表示同一对象随时间增减变化，用折线统计图；表示各部分数量与总数的关系，用扇形统计图。只含一组数据的是单式统计图，含两组或多组数据的是复式统计图，便于对照；扇形统计图不适合比较不同总数背景下的绝对数量。
读图要防止误读：检查纵轴是否从 $0$ 开始、单位和每格数值是否看清、复式图的图例是否对应。例：某班共有 $40$ 人，喜欢篮球的有 $16$ 人，则扇形图中篮球所占百分比为 $16\div40\times100\%=40\%$，对应圆心角为 $360^\circ\times40\%=144^\circ$；其余部分合计占 $60\%$，总和为 $100\%$。
derivationEn: A statistical chart draws organized data as a figure for easy reading, comparison and analysis. Before reading a chart, check the title, what the horizontal and vertical axes represent, the unit, and how much one grid square stands for; the same data drawn in different charts emphasizes different information. The common charts in primary school are the bar chart, the line chart and the pie chart.

A bar chart uses the length of bars to represent amounts: the longer the bar, the larger the amount. To compare amounts, all bars must be measured from the same baseline (usually $0$); otherwise differences in length are exaggerated. Read a value as 'number of grid squares $\times$ value per square', not as the number of squares alone. A multiple bar chart places two or more sets of bars side by side for comparison.

A line chart joins data points in time order with segments: a rising segment means an increase, a falling segment a decrease; when the time intervals on the horizontal axis are equal, a steeper segment means a faster change. It is suited to trends, but the segments between adjacent data points are only a guide and do not determine the actual values between those times; exact values must be read from the points or the data table.

A pie chart takes the total as the whole circle, namely $100\%$, and each sector represents one part. If a part has amount $m$ and the total is $N$ ($N>0$), its percentage of the total is $\frac{m}{N}\times100\%$, and the corresponding central angle is $360^\circ\times\frac{m}{N}$. All percentages add up to $100\%$ and all central angles to $360^\circ$; to recover an amount from a percentage, the total must also be known.

Choose a chart according to the purpose: to compare amounts of different categories, use a bar chart; to show how one quantity rises and falls over time, use a line chart; to show the relation of parts to the whole, use a pie chart. A single chart contains one data set, while a multiple chart contains two or more sets for comparison; a pie chart is not suitable for comparing absolute amounts when the totals differ.

Guard against misreading: check whether the vertical axis starts at $0$, whether the unit and the value per grid square are clear, and whether the legend of a multiple chart is matched correctly. Example: in a class of $40$ students, $16$ like basketball, so in a pie chart basketball accounts for $16\div40\times100\%=40\%$, with central angle $360^\circ\times40\%=144^\circ$; the remaining parts account for $60\%$, and the total is $100\%$.

formulas.latex: \text{条形统计图：直条的长短表示数量的多少}
formulas.note: 能清楚地看出数量的多少，最适合比较谁多谁少。
formulas.noteEn: Shows amounts clearly; the best choice for comparing more and less.

formulas.latex: \text{折线统计图：数量的多少} + \text{增减变化的趋势}
formulas.note: 折线往上走就是增加、往下走就是减少；看变化趋势它最拿手。
formulas.noteEn: A rising line means increase, a falling line means decrease; no chart shows a trend better.

formulas.latex: \text{扇形统计图：各部分数量与总数之间的关系}
formulas.note: 整个圆表示总数 100%，每个扇形表示一部分占总数的百分之几。
formulas.noteEn: The circle is the total 100%, and each sector is one part's share of the whole.

formulas.latex: \text{每部分占总数的百分比} = \dfrac{\text{该部分的数量}}{\text{总数}} \times 100\%
formulas.note: 所有部分的百分比相加正好等于 100%，可以用来检查扇形统计图画得对不对。
formulas.noteEn: All the percentages add up to 100%, which checks whether a pie chart is drawn correctly.

properties: 条形统计图能清楚地看出数量的多少：直条越长，数量越多。
折线统计图不但能看出数量的多少，还能清楚地看出数量增减变化的趋势。
扇形统计图能清楚地反映出各部分数量与总数之间的关系；各部分的百分比之和是 100%。
只画一组数据的叫单式统计图，两组或多组数据画在一起的是复式统计图，便于比较。
画统计图的步骤：收集数据、整理数据、制成统计表、画出统计图。
propertiesEn: A bar chart shows amounts clearly: the longer the bar, the larger the amount.
A line chart shows not only the amounts but also the trend of increase and decrease.
A pie chart shows the relation between each part and the whole; the percentages add up to 100%.
A single chart shows one set of data; a multiple chart shows two or more sets together for easy comparison.
Steps for drawing a chart: collect the data, sort the data, make a table, draw the chart.

examples.problem: 下面三种情况，各选用哪种统计图最合适？① 统计全班同学最喜欢的水果各有几人；② 记录某地一周每天的最高气温，想看出气温的升降变化；③ 统计全班同学各种血型的人数各占总人数的百分之几。
examples.solution: ① 要比出各种水果人数的多少，用**条形统计图**；② 要看一周气温的增减变化趋势，用**折线统计图**；③ 要看各部分数量与总数之间的关系（百分比），用**扇形统计图**。

examples.problem: 六（1）班共有 40 人，其中喜欢打篮球的有 16 人。在扇形统计图中，喜欢打篮球的人数对应的扇形占总数的百分之几？
examples.solution: 各部分占总数的百分比 = 该部分的数量 ÷ 总数 × 100% = $16 \div 40 \times 100\% = 0.4 \times 100\% = 40\%$。所以喜欢打篮球的扇形占整个圆的 40%，其余部分合计占 60%，加起来正好 100%。

average-elementary.definition:
老师说「这次全班数学平均分是 85 分」，跳绳比赛要算「平均每人跳多少个」……这里的**平均数**，是代表一组数据**整体水平**的数：把所有的数据先**合起来**，再**平均分**给每一份，就得到平均数。

求平均数一般有两种办法。一种是**移多补少**：把多的移一些给少的，直到每一份都一样多，这个一样多的数就是平均数；另一种是**计算法**：**平均数 = 总数量 ÷ 总份数**。例如 3、4、8、9 四个数的平均数 $=(3+4+8+9)\div 4=24\div 4=6$。

平均数代表一组数据的整体水平，但它**不一定**等于其中某个数据（上面的 6 就不在 3、4、8、9 里），它总落在最小的数与最大的数之间。**平均数容易受极端值影响**：如果一个班里有一位同学个子特别高，全班的平均身高就会被这个「极端值」拉高，这时用平均数代表全班的水平就要小心一些。

平均数在生活中用处很多：平均分、平均身高、平均速度。注意**平均速度 = 总路程 ÷ 总时间**，不能把几个速度直接相加再除以个数——要先算「一共走了多远」，再算「一共用了多少时间」。
average-elementary.definitionEn:
A teacher says, 'The class average in maths is 85.' A skipping contest asks, 'How many skips per person on average?' The **average** stands for the **overall level** of a data set: add the data together, then share the total equally among all the items.

There are two ways to find it. **'Move more to fill less'**: shift amounts from the larger values to the smaller ones until all are equal; that common value is the average. Or **compute**: **average = total amount ÷ number of items**. The average of 3, 4, 8 and 9 is $(3+4+8+9)\div 4=24\div 4=6$.

The average represents the overall level, but it **need not equal any of the data values** (6 is not among 3, 4, 8, 9); it always lies between the smallest and the largest value. An **extreme value strongly affects the average**: one very tall pupil pulls the average height up, so read such an average with care.

Averages appear everywhere: average score, average height, average speed. Note that **average speed = total distance ÷ total time**; you cannot simply average the separate speeds—first find the whole distance, then the whole time.
derivation: 平均数表示一组数据的整体水平：把总数量平均分给总份数。若数据是 $a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n$，则平均数为 $\bar{x}=(a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_n)\div n$。这里总份数 $n$ 必须与总数量对应，且 $n>0$；各数据的单位要相同。
例：3、4、8、9 的总和是 $3+4+8+9=24$，总份数 $n=4$，所以平均数 $=24\div4=6$。6 并不在这四个数中，说明平均数不一定等于某个原始数据；它相当于把多的移给少的，使 4 份都变成 6。
平均数一定在最小值和最大值之间。设最小值为 $m$、最大值为 $M$，则每个数据都不小于 $m$、不大于 $M$，所以 $nm\le a_1+\cdots+a_n\le nM$。两边同时除以 $n$，得 $m\le\bar{x}\le M$。只有当所有数据都等于 $m$ 或都等于 $M$ 时，才取到端点。
逆用公式：总数量 $=$ 平均数 $\times$ 总份数。若 5 个数的平均数是 12，则总和为 $5\times12=60$；若前 4 个数的和是 47，则第 5 个数是 $60-47=13$。检验：$(47+13)\div5=60\div5=12$，符合要求。
平均数容易受极端值影响：3、4、8、9 的平均数是 6；若把 9 换成 90，总和变成 $3+4+8+90=105$，平均数变成 $105\div4=26.25$，被极端值拉高了。因此当数据中有特别大或特别小的值时，要说清平均数是否还能代表整体水平。
平均速度要用总路程除以总时间。上山速度 2 千米/时，下山速度 6 千米/时，若两段路程都是 $d$，则总路程为 $2d$，总时间为 $d/2+d/6=2d/3$，平均速度 $=2d\div(2d/3)=3$ 千米/时，不是 $(2+6)\div2=4$。慢速那段用时更长，不能把几个速度直接算术平均；只有各段时间相等时才能那样做。
derivationEn: The average describes the overall level of a data set: share the total amount equally among all items. For data $a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n$, the average is $\bar{x}=(a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_n)\div n$. The number $n$ of items must match the total, $n>0$, and all data must use the same unit.

Example: the total of 3, 4, 8 and 9 is $3+4+8+9=24$, and $n=4$, so the average is $24\div4=6$. Since 6 is not one of the four values, an average need not equal any original data value; it is the common value obtained by moving excess to cover deficits until all four items equal 6.

An average always lies between the minimum and the maximum. Let $m$ be the minimum and $M$ the maximum; every value is at least $m$ and at most $M$, so $nm\le a_1+\cdots+a_n\le nM$. Dividing by $n$ gives $m\le\bar{x}\le M$. Equality at an endpoint occurs only when every value equals $m$ or every value equals $M$.

Use the formula in reverse: total $=$ average $\times$ number of items. If five numbers have average 12, their total is $5\times12=60$; if the first four sum to 47, the fifth number is $60-47=13$. Check: $(47+13)\div5=60\div5=12$, as required.

The average is easily affected by extreme values: the average of 3, 4, 8 and 9 is 6; replacing 9 by 90 changes the total to $3+4+8+90=105$ and the average to $105\div4=26.25$, pulled upward. So when a data set contains an unusually large or small value, state whether the average still represents the overall level.

Average speed is total distance divided by total time. If the uphill speed is 2 km/h and the downhill speed is 6 km/h over the same distance $d$, the total distance is $2d$ and the total time is $d/2+d/6=2d/3$, so the average speed is $2d\div(2d/3)=3$ km/h, not $(2+6)\div2=4$. The slower part takes more time, so separate speeds cannot be averaged directly; that is valid only when the times are equal.

formulas.note: 求平均数：先把一组数据全部加起来求出总数量，再除以数据的个数（总份数）。
formulas.noteEn: To find an average, add all the data to get the total, then divide by how many items there are.

formulas.note: 3、4、8、9 的平均数是 6；6 并不在这四个数里，说明平均数不一定等于原来某个数据。
formulas.noteEn: The average of 3, 4, 8, 9 is 6; 6 is not among them, so an average need not equal any original value.

formulas.note: 例：上山每小时 2 千米、下山每小时 6 千米，往返的平均速度是 3 千米/时，而不是 4 千米/时。
formulas.noteEn: Example: 2 km/h uphill and 6 km/h downhill give an average speed of 3 km/h, not 4 km/h.

formulas.latex: \text{移多补少：把多的移一些给少的，使每份一样多}
formulas.note: 这是求平均数最直观的办法；移完以后每份一样多的那个数，就是平均数。
formulas.noteEn: The most intuitive method: move from the bigger to the smaller until all are equal; that common value is the average.

properties: 平均数 = 总数量 ÷ 总份数；求平均数先求和，再除以数据的个数。
平均数代表一组数据的整体水平，它不一定等于其中任何一个数据。
平均数一定在最小的数据和最大的数据之间（可以与它们相等）。
平均数容易受极端值影响：个别特别大或特别小的数据会把平均数拉高或拉低。
平均速度 = 总路程 ÷ 总时间，不能把几个速度直接平均。
propertiesEn: Average = total amount ÷ number of items; add the data first, then divide by how many there are.
The average stands for the overall level of a data set and need not equal any single data value.
The average always lies between the smallest and the largest value (endpoints included).
The average is easily affected by extreme values: one very large or very small value pulls it up or down.
Average speed = total distance ÷ total time; the separate speeds cannot be averaged directly.

examples.problem: 四（1）班第一小组同学一分钟跳绳的成绩是 132、145、128、135 个。这组成绩的平均数是多少？
examples.solution: 总数量 $=132+145+128+135=540$（个），总份数是 4，所以平均数 $=540\div 4=135$（个）。它表示这个小组一分钟跳绳的整体水平大约是 135 个。（135 恰好等于其中一个数据，但平均数并不一定等于某个数据。）

examples.problem: 小明上山时每小时走 2 千米，沿原路下山时每小时走 6 千米。有人说「往返的平均速度就是 $(2+6)\div 2=4$ 千米/时」，对吗？
examples.solution: 不对。假设山路长 6 千米：上山用 $6\div 2=3$（小时），下山用 $6\div 6=1$（小时）；往返的总路程 $=6+6=12$（千米），总时间 $=3+1=4$（小时），所以平均速度 $=$ 总路程 $\div$ 总时间 $=12\div 4=3$（千米/时），不是 4 千米/时。

possibility-elementary.definition:
有些事情**一定**会发生，比如早晨太阳从东方升起；有些事情**不可能**发生，比如太阳从西方升起；还有些事情**可能**发生、也可能不发生，比如「明天会下雨吗」「随手一摸，摸出的是什么颜色的球」。

判断一件事属于哪一种，要先看清**条件**：抛一枚普通的硬币，「正面朝上」和「反面朝上」都可能；掷一枚正常的骰子，「掷出 7 点」是不可能事件，「掷出 3 点」是可能事件。条件变了，结论也会跟着变。

**可能性有大小**。袋子里红球多、白球少，闭上眼睛随便摸一个，摸到红球的**可能性大**，摸到白球的**可能性小**。一般地，**数量越多，可能性越大；数量越少，可能性越小**。

可能性的大小还可以用**分数**表示：袋子里有 3 个红球和 1 个白球，一共 4 个球，每个球被摸到的机会一样，那么摸到红球的可能性是 $\frac{3}{4}$，摸到白球的可能性是 $\frac{1}{4}$。两个人做游戏要**公平**，就得让双方获胜的可能性相等；可能性不相等，游戏就不公平。
possibility-elementary.definitionEn:
Some things are **certain** to happen, like the Sun rising in the east in the morning; some are **impossible**, like the Sun rising in the west; and some **may or may not** happen, like 'Will it rain tomorrow?' or 'What colour ball will I draw?'

To decide which case an event belongs to, look at the **conditions**. With an ordinary coin, heads and tails are both possible, while 'throwing 7' is impossible; with a normal die, 'rolling a 7' is impossible and 'rolling a 3' is possible. Change the conditions, and the answer changes too.

**Chances have sizes.** If a bag holds many red balls and few white ones, a blind draw is more likely to give red. In general, **more items mean a greater chance; fewer items mean a smaller chance**.

A fraction can tell how big a chance is: with 3 red and 1 white ball, 4 balls in all, every ball equally likely to be drawn, the chance of drawing red is $\frac{3}{4}$ and of drawing white is $\frac{1}{4}$. For a game to be **fair**, both players must have equal chances; if the chances differ, the game is unfair.
derivation: 在给定条件下，事件的发生分为三种：一定发生（必然事件）、可能发生也可能不发生（随机事件）、不可能发生（不可能事件）。例如掷一枚正常骰子，「掷出 3 点」是可能的，「掷出 7 点」是不可能的；抛一枚普通硬币，「正面朝上」是可能的，「同时正面和反面朝上」是不可能的。判断前要先写清条件。
在有限个等可能结果的情形，每个结果出现的可能性相同，事件 $A$ 的可能性可用分数表示：$P(A)=\frac{\text{有利于 }A\text{ 的结果数}}{\text{所有等可能结果总数}}$。袋中 3 个红球、1 个白球，共 4 个球，大小质地相同、任意摸一个，则 $P(\text{红})=\frac34$，$P(\text{白})=\frac14$。
在这个等可能模型里，所有可能结果的概率之和为 1：$\frac34+\frac14=1$。这也说明「一定」对应 1，「不可能」对应 0；任何事件的可能性都在 0 与 1 之间。比较大小看分子（分母相同）：$\frac34>\frac14$，所以摸到红球的可能性大；在总数相同（或各结果等可能且总数不变）时，某种结果对应的数量越多，可能性越大。
游戏公平当且仅当双方获胜的可能性相等。上述 3 红 1 白的袋子里，甲摸红赢、乙摸白赢，$P(\text{甲赢})=\frac34\ne\frac14=P(\text{乙赢})$，游戏不公平，甲占优势。若要公平，可增加 2 个白球，使红、白各 3 个，双方获胜概率都是 $\frac36=\frac12$。
条件改变，可能性也随之改变。若第一次摸出红球后不放回，袋中剩 2 红 1 白，共 3 个球，第二次摸到红球的概率变为 $\frac23$，摸到白球变为 $\frac13$；若放回，则仍是 $\frac34$ 与 $\frac14$。所以「摸两次」的问题必须说明放回还是不放回。
注意：「可能」不等于「可能性是 $\frac12$」。只有所有结果等可能时才能用「有利结果数÷总数」；「明天下雨」和「明天不下雨」两个结果并不等可能，不能各算 50%。可能性大小由数量或面积等比例决定，不能只看有几种结果。
derivationEn: Under given conditions an event is certain (must happen), random (may or may not happen) or impossible (cannot happen). With a fair die, rolling a 3 is possible while rolling a 7 is impossible; with an ordinary coin, heads is possible while showing heads and tails at once is impossible. State the conditions before classifying.

When there are finitely many equally likely outcomes, each outcome has the same chance, and the probability of an event $A$ is the fraction $P(A)=\frac{\text{number of outcomes favourable to }A}{\text{total number of equally likely outcomes}}$. A bag with 3 red and 1 white ball, all identical in size and texture, gives $P(\text{red})=\frac34$ and $P(\text{white})=\frac14$ for one blind draw.

In this equally likely model, the probabilities of all possible outcomes sum to 1: $\frac34+\frac14=1$. Hence 'certain' corresponds to 1 and 'impossible' to 0, and every probability lies between 0 and 1. With equal denominators, compare numerators: $\frac34>\frac14$, so red is more likely; when the total is the same (or the other conditions are unchanged), more items of a given kind mean a greater chance.

A game is fair exactly when both players have equal chances. In the 3-red, 1-white bag, if A wins on red and B on white, $P(\text{A wins})=\frac34\ne\frac14=P(\text{B wins})$, so the game is unfair and favours A. To make it fair, add 2 white balls so that there are 3 of each colour; both winning probabilities become $\frac36=\frac12$.

Changing the conditions changes the probabilities. If the first draw is red and the ball is not replaced, the bag holds 2 red and 1 white, so on the second draw $P(\text{red})=\frac23$ and $P(\text{white})=\frac13$; with replacement they remain $\frac34$ and $\frac14$. Every two-draw question must therefore state whether draws are with or without replacement.

Caution: 'possible' does not mean probability $\frac12$. The rule 'favourable outcomes ÷ total outcomes' applies only when all outcomes are equally likely; 'rain tomorrow' and 'no rain tomorrow' are not equally likely and cannot each be assigned 50%. Probability is determined by proportions such as counts or areas, not merely by how many outcomes are listed.

formulas.note: 事情的发生有三种情况：一定（必然发生）、可能（也许发生、也许不发生）、不可能（绝不会发生）。
formulas.noteEn: Three cases: certain (must happen), possible (may or may not happen) and impossible (never happens).

formulas.latex: \text{数量越多} \Rightarrow \text{可能性越大};\qquad \text{数量越少} \Rightarrow \text{可能性越小}
formulas.note: 摸球、转转盘、抽签都用这一条来判断可能性的大小。
formulas.noteEn: Drawing balls, spinning a wheel or drawing lots—all judged by this rule.

formulas.note: 袋中 3 个红球、1 个白球，共 4 个球：摸到红球的可能性是 3/4，摸到白球的可能性是 1/4。
formulas.noteEn: With 3 red and 1 white ball (4 in all): drawing red has chance 3/4, drawing white 1/4.

formulas.latex: \text{游戏公平} \iff \text{双方获胜的可能性相等}
formulas.note: 可能性相等，游戏才公平；不相等就不公平，可能性大的那一方占便宜。
formulas.noteEn: A game is fair exactly when both sides have an equal chance; unequal chances favour the side with the larger chance.

properties: 一件事的发生有三种情况：一定、可能、不可能。
数量越多，可能性越大；数量越少，可能性越小。
可能性的大小可以用分数表示：袋中 3 个红球、1 个白球时，摸到红球的可能性是 3/4，摸到白球的可能性是 1/4。
游戏规则公平的条件是各方获胜的可能性相等；可能性不相等，游戏就不公平。
「一定」和「不可能」是两种确定的情况；比较可能性大小，是就那些「可能发生、也可能不发生」的事情来说的。
propertiesEn: An event may be certain, possible or impossible.
The more items there are, the greater the chance; the fewer, the smaller.
A chance can be written as a fraction: with 3 red and 1 white ball, drawing red has chance 3/4 and white 1/4.
A game is fair exactly when all sides have an equal chance of winning; unequal chances make it unfair.
'Certain' and 'impossible' are settled outcomes; comparing chances applies to events that may or may not happen.

examples.problem: 判断下面的说法对不对：① 明天可能下雨；② 太阳不可能从西边升起；③ 抛一枚普通硬币，一定正面朝上。
examples.solution: ① 对。「明天可能下雨」表示明天下雨和不下雨都有可能，用「可能」描述。② 对。太阳从西边升起是绝不会发生的事情，用「不可能」描述。③ 不对。抛硬币时正面朝上只是**可能**发生，反面朝上也同样可能，两种结果的可能性相等，不能说「一定」。

examples.problem: 袋子里有 3 个红球和 1 个白球（大小、形状和质地都一样），闭上眼睛任意摸出一个球。① 摸到红球的可能性大，还是摸到白球的可能性大？② 摸到红球、摸到白球的可能性各是几分之几？③ 用这个袋子做「摸到红球甲赢、摸到白球乙赢」的游戏，公平吗？
examples.solution: ① 一共有 $3+1=4$ 个球，红球比白球多，所以摸到红球的**可能性大**。② 每个球被摸到的机会一样：摸到红球的可能性是 $\frac{3}{4}$，摸到白球的可能性是 $\frac{1}{4}$。③ 因为 $\frac{3}{4}\ne\frac{1}{4}$，甲、乙获胜的可能性不相等，所以这个游戏**不公平**（甲赢的机会大）。

chicken-rabbit.definition:
大约 1500 年前，我国数学名著《孙子算经》里有这样一道题：「今有雉兔同笼，上有三十五头，下有九十四足，问雉兔各几何？」意思是：笼子里有鸡和兔一共 35 只，从上面数有 35 个头，从下面数有 94 只脚，鸡和兔各有多少只？这就是有名的**鸡兔同笼**问题。

解决它的巧妙办法叫**假设法**，口诀是「**先假设，再比较，后调整**」。假设 35 只**全是鸡**：每只鸡 2 只脚，一共 $35\times 2=70$ 只脚；可实际有 94 只脚，比 70 多了 $94-70=24$ 只脚。为什么会少算？因为把一只兔当成鸡来算，就少算了 $4-2=2$ 只脚。少算的 24 只脚里有多少个 2，就有多少只兔：$24\div 2=12$，所以兔有 12 只，鸡有 $35-12=23$ 只。验算：$23\times 2+12\times 4=46+48=94$（只脚），$23+12=35$（个头），完全符合。

也可以假设 35 只**全是兔**：一共 $35\times 4=140$ 只脚，比 94 多 $140-94=46$ 只；每把一只鸡当成兔就多算 2 只脚，所以鸡有 $46\div 2=23$ 只，兔有 $35-23=12$ 只，答案一样。除了假设法，还可以用**列表法**（一个一个试，直到脚数对上）和**方程法**（设鸡有 $x$ 只，兔就有 $35-x$ 只，列方程 $2x+4(35-x)=94$），这些方法以后都会学到。

鸡兔同笼问题的核心思想是**假设—比较—调整**：先大胆假设一个简单情况，和实际比一比，看看差多少；再想一想差的原因——每差 2 只脚，就说明有一只兔被当成了鸡；把差的数除以 2，就调整出了正确答案。生活中很多类似的问题（比如停车场里的自行车和汽车各有多少辆）都能用这个思路解决。
chicken-rabbit.definitionEn:
About 1500 years ago the Chinese classic *Sunzi Suanjing* posed a famous puzzle: 'In one cage pheasants and rabbits, above 35 heads, below 94 feet—how many of each?' In modern words: chickens and rabbits together number 35, and their feet total 94; how many chickens and how many rabbits are there? This is the classic **chicken-and-rabbit problem**.

The clever method is **'assume, compare, adjust'**. Suppose all 35 animals are chickens: $35\times 2=70$ feet, but there are 94, which is $94-70=24$ feet more. Why the shortage? Counting a rabbit as a chicken loses $4-2=2$ feet. The missing 24 feet contain as many 2's as there are rabbits: $24\div 2=12$, so there are 12 rabbits and $35-12=23$ chickens. Check: $23\times 2+12\times 4=46+48=94$ feet and $23+12=35$ heads—everything fits.

Assuming all 35 are rabbits works too: $35\times 4=140$ feet, which is $140-94=46$ too many; each chicken counted as a rabbit adds 2 extra feet, so there are $46\div 2=23$ chickens and $35-23=12$ rabbits—the same answer. A **table** (try values until the feet match) or an **equation** (let the chickens be $x$ and the rabbits $35-x$, then $2x+4(35-x)=94$) also work; those methods come later in school.

The core idea is **assume–compare–adjust**: guess a simple case, compare with the real data, see the gap, then remember that every 2 feet of gap means one rabbit mistaken for a chicken, and divide the gap by 2. Many everyday problems—for instance, how many bicycles and how many cars are in a car park—give way to the same idea.
derivation: 设鸡有 $c$ 只、兔有 $r$ 只，共有 $h$ 个头、$f$ 只脚。每只鸡 2 只脚，每只兔 4 只脚，所以 $h=c+r$，$f=2c+4r$，且 $c,r$ 都是非负整数。由 $f=2(c+r)+2r=2h+2r$ 可知 $2h\le f\le4h$，并且 $f-2h$ 必须是偶数；不满足这些条件时无解。
假设 $h$ 只全是鸡：一共有 $2h$ 只脚，比实际 $f$ 少了 $f-2h$ 只。每把一只鸡换成一只兔，脚数就增加 $4-2=2$ 只。因此兔的只数 $r=(f-2h)\div2$，鸡的只数 $c=h-r$。这就是「假设—比较—调整」：先假设，再比较差多少，最后按每差 2 只脚对应一只兔来调整。
也可以假设全是兔：$h$ 只兔一共有 $4h$ 只脚，比实际 $f$ 多了 $4h-f$ 只。每把一只兔换成一只鸡，脚数减少 2 只，所以鸡有 $c=(4h-f)\div2$ 只，兔有 $r=h-c$ 只。对 $h=35,f=94$，$c=(140-94)\div2=23$，$r=12$，与假设全鸡得到的答案一致，可以互相检验。
还要检查答案是否合理：若 $h=10,f=25$，$f$ 是奇数，$f-2h=5$ 不能被 2 整除，没有整数解；若 $h=10,f=50$，$r=(50-20)\div2=15>h$，会算出鸡为 $-5$ 只，不可能。$h=10$ 时，$f=20$ 给出 $r=0,c=10$；$f=40$ 给出 $r=10,c=0$。所以答案必须满足 $0\le r\le h$。

应用：自行车和汽车共 10 辆，一共有 28 个轮子。假设全是自行车，轮子有 $10\times2=20$ 个，比 28 少 8 个；每辆汽车多 2 个轮子，所以汽车有 $8\div2=4$ 辆，自行车有 $10-4=6$ 辆。验算：$6\times2+4\times4=12+16=28$ 个轮子，$6+4=10$ 辆车。列方程 $2x+4(10-x)=28$ 也能得到 $x=6$，与假设法一致。
derivationEn: Let there be $c$ chickens and $r$ rabbits, with $h$ heads and $f$ feet. Each chicken has 2 feet and each rabbit 4, so $h=c+r$ and $f=2c+4r$, where $c$ and $r$ are non-negative integers. Since $f=2(c+r)+2r=2h+2r$, we must have $2h\le f\le4h$ and $f-2h$ even; if these conditions fail, there is no solution.

Assume all $h$ animals are chickens: they have $2h$ feet, which is $f-2h$ fewer than the actual number. Replacing one chicken by one rabbit adds $4-2=2$ feet. Therefore the number of rabbits is $r=(f-2h)\div2$, and the number of chickens is $c=h-r$. This is the 'assume–compare–adjust' method: suppose, compare the gap, then adjust using the fact that every gap of 2 feet means one rabbit.

For $h=35$ and $f=94$: assuming all chickens gives $35\times2=70$ feet, a gap of $94-70=24$. Each rabbit adds 2 feet, so there are $24\div2=12$ rabbits and $35-12=23$ chickens. Check: $23\times2+12\times4=46+48=94$ feet and $23+12=35$ heads, exactly as required.

Assume all are rabbits instead: $h$ rabbits have $4h$ feet, which is $4h-f$ too many. Replacing one rabbit by one chicken removes 2 feet, so there are $c=(4h-f)\div2$ chickens and $r=h-c$ rabbits. For $h=35,f=94$, $c=(140-94)\div2=23$ and $r=12$, the same answer as assuming all chickens, which serves as a check.

Also check that the answer is feasible: if $h=10$ and $f=25$, then $f$ is odd and $f-2h=5$ is not divisible by 2, so there is no integer solution; if $h=10$ and $f=50$, then $r=(50-20)\div2=15>h$, which would give $c=-5$, impossible. For $h=10$, $f=20$ gives $r=0,c=10$, while $f=40$ gives $r=10,c=0$. Hence any answer must satisfy $0\le r\le h$.

Application: 10 bicycles and cars have 28 wheels in total. Assume all are bicycles: $10\times2=20$ wheels, a gap of 8; each car adds 2 wheels, so there are $8\div2=4$ cars and $10-4=6$ bicycles. Check: $6\times2+4\times4=12+16=28$ wheels and $6+4=10$ vehicles. The equation $2x+4(10-x)=28$ gives $x=6$, the same result as the assumption method.

formulas.note: 假设 35 只全是鸡，每只鸡 2 只脚，先算出一个「假设的」脚数。
formulas.noteEn: Assume all 35 are chickens, 2 feet each, and compute the 'pretend' total number of feet.

formulas.note: 实际脚数比假设多 24 只；每把一只兔当成鸡就少算 2 只脚，所以差的脚数 ÷ 2 就是兔的只数。
formulas.noteEn: There are 24 feet more than assumed; each rabbit read as a chicken hides 2 feet, so the gap ÷ 2 gives the number of rabbits.

formulas.note: 用总头数减去兔的只数，就得到鸡的只数。
formulas.noteEn: Subtract the rabbits from the total number of heads to get the chickens.

formulas.note: 反过来假设全是兔，也能算出答案，可以用来互相检验。
formulas.noteEn: Assuming all are rabbits gives the same answer and serves as a check.

formulas.note: 把答案代回题目验算：脚数 94、头数 $23+12=35$，完全符合，答案正确。
formulas.noteEn: Check by substitution: 94 feet and $23+12=35$ heads match the problem exactly.

properties: 鸡有 2 只脚，兔有 4 只脚，每只兔比每只鸡多 2 只脚——这是「调整」的关键。
假设全是鸡时：兔 =（总脚数 − 头数 × 2）÷ 2；假设全是兔时：鸡 =（头数 × 4 − 总脚数）÷ 2。
解题思路是「假设—比较—调整」：先假设、再比较差多少、最后按「每差 2 只脚对应一只兔」来调整。
算完要用头数和脚数两个条件各验算一次，答案才保险。
列表法、画图法、方程法都能解决鸡兔同笼问题；道理明白了，用哪种方法都可以。
propertiesEn: A chicken has 2 feet and a rabbit has 4, so every rabbit has 2 feet more than a chicken—the key to adjusting.
If all are assumed to be chickens: rabbits = (total feet − heads × 2) ÷ 2; if all are assumed to be rabbits: chickens = (heads × 4 − total feet) ÷ 2.
The method is assume–compare–adjust: suppose, compare the gap, then adjust using 'a gap of 2 feet means one rabbit'.
Always check the answer against both the number of heads and the number of feet.
Tables, pictures and equations all solve the problem; once you see why it works, any method is fine.

examples.problem: 笼子里有鸡和兔共 35 只，一共有 94 只脚。鸡和兔各有多少只？
停车场里停着自行车和汽车共 10 辆，每辆自行车有 2 个轮子，每辆汽车有 4 个轮子，一共 28 个轮子。自行车和汽车各有多少辆？
examples.solution: 假设 10 辆全是自行车：轮子 $=10\times 2=20$（个），比 28 少 $28-20=8$（个）。把一辆汽车当成自行车会少算 $4-2=2$ 个轮子，所以汽车有 $8\div 2=4$（辆），自行车有 $10-4=6$（辆）。验算：$6\times 2+4\times 4=12+16=28$（个轮子），$6+4=10$（辆），符合题意。
